Glancing up, she saw her husband at a second-floor window of the opium den.
He vanished from the window immediately, and X12 was sure that something was wrong.
She tried to enter the building, but her path was blocked by a lascar, who owns the opium den.
She fetched the police, but they did not find X9; the room behind the window was the lair of a dirty, disfigured beggar, known to the police as X13.
The police were about to put her story down as a mistake of some kind when X12 noticed a box of wooden toy bricks that her husband said he would buy for their son.

A further search turned up some of X7's clothes; later, his coat, with the pockets stuffed with hundreds of pennies and halfpennies, was found on the bank of the X14, just below the building's back window.
Bloodstains are found on the windowsill and bedroom floor.
X13 was arrested at once but would say nothing, except to deny any knowledge of X7, and also vehemently resisted any attempt to make him wash.
X5 was initially quite convinced that X7 had been murdered, and that X15 was involved, so he investigated the den in disguise.

He and X2 return to X7's home, to a surprise - it is several days after the disappearance, but on that day, X12 had received a letter from her husband in his own handwriting, with his signet ring enclosed, telling her not to worry.
This forces X5 to reconsider his conclusions, leading him eventually to an extraordinary solution.
X5 and X2 go the police station where X13 is held; X5 brings a bath sponge, which he uses to wash the sleeping X15's dirty face and reveal him as X6.
X9 has been living a double life, as a respectable businessman and as a squalid beggar.
In his youth, he had been an actor before becoming a newspaper reporter.

To research an article, he had disguised himself as a beggar for a short time, and was able to collect a surprising amount of money due to a skillset uncommon to beggars; his acting skills enabled him to emulate a more sympathetic character with make-up, as well as provide a repertoire of witty dialogue with which to entertain passers-by to offer coins — in this way, he was just as much a street performer as he was a beggar.
Some time later, he was saddled with a large unexpected debt, so he returned to the street to beg for several days to pay it off.
His newspaper salary was very small and, tempted by the much larger returns of begging, he eventually became a "professional" beggar.
His takings were large enough (averaging over £700 a year, ) that he was able to establish himself as a country gentleman, marry well, and begin a respectable family.
His wife and children never knew what he did for a living, and when he was arrested, he feared exposure more than prison or the gallows.
Since no murder has been committed, he is released, and X5 and the police agree to keep X9's secret on the condition that no more is heard of X13.

title: The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle
label: The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle
sentences: As X1 prepares for Christmas, newspapers report the theft of a near-priceless gemstone, the "X2", from the X3's hotel suite.
The police arrest X4, a plumber with a criminal record who was in the Countess's room repairing a fireplace grate.

Meanwhile, at X5 finds X6 contemplating a battered old hat brought to him by X7, a commissionaire who seeks X8's help in returning it and a Christmas goose to their rightful owners after he found them the previous night in the street after a scuffle.
A tag on the goose reading "For X9" is of little assistance, as the name is a very common one.
Ultimately, X7 takes the goose home for dinner and X8 keeps the hat to study as an intellectual exercise, deducing X10's age, social standing, intellect, and domestic status.
An excited X7 bursts in, having found the stolen gem in the goose's crop.
That evening when X10 appears in response to advertisements placed by X8 in the X1 newspapers, X8 returns his hat and offers him a new goose, which he happily accepts.
X10's refusal to take the original bird's entrails leads X8 to believe that he knew nothing of the theft and that he has been truthful in his claim of having purchased the goose at a pub.
X8 and X11 visit the pub, whose proprietor states that he bought the goose and several others from a dealer in X12.
However, the dealer refuses to help, complaining that he has been repeatedly pestered by another man about geese he sold to the pub.
Realising that he is not the only one aware of the goose's importance, X8 tricks the dealer into revealing that it was supplied to him by its breeder, a X13 of X14.
The pestering man visits the stall and identifies himself to X8 as X15, head attendant at the hotel from which the gem was stolen, who had testified that he found it missing.

Upon being taken to X16 and shown the gem, a remorseful X17 admits that he and his accomplice, the Countess's maid, had contrived to steal it and frame X18, whose criminal past would make him an easy scapegoat.
During a visit to his sister, X19 had concealed the gem by feeding it to a goose she had promised him as a gift, but confused the bird with another.
By the time he realised his mistake, his goose had already been sold.
As it is Christmas, X8 takes pity on X17 and allows him to flee the country, concluding that the man is too frightened by what happened to offend again.
X8 is confident that the case against X18 will be dismissed for lack of evidence once X17 fails to appear in court as a prosecution witness.

title: The Adventure of the Speckled Band
label: The Adventure of the Speckled Band
sentences: In April 1883, X1 and X2 rise early one morning to meet a young woman named X3, who is in great fear of her life.
She explains that her mother married her stepfather, X4, in X5 when X6 and her twin sister X7 were two years old.
X8 is the impoverished sole survivor of a formerly wealthy but ill-tempered, violent, and amoral aristocratic Anglo-Saxon family in X9.
He had served time in an Indian prison for killing his Indian butler in a rage.
Afterwards, X10 had moved to X11 and retired after X6's mother was killed in a railway accident eight years prior.
The sisters lived at the heavily mortgaged and debt ridden X10 estate of X12's violent temper and physical strength make him a terror in the local village.
The sisters did not live happily, but when X7 got engaged two years prior, things promised to improve.
Shortly before her wedding day, X7 confided in X6 that she had heard a low whistle in the night.
That same night, X6 was startled out of bed by her sister's scream.
X6 found X7 at her door, warning of "the speckled band" shortly before dying.
The official inquest was unable to determine the cause of death: the room was securely locked both inside and outside, and the doctors could find no poison.
Two years later, it was X6's turn to get engaged.
However, when X10 started repairs outside the house, she had to move into X7's old room.
One night, she heard the whistle that heralded her sister's death; terrified, she approached X13 the next day.
After X13 agrees to take the case, he is visited by X10, who threatens to harm him if he interferes.
Undaunted, X13 leaves for the courthouse to examine X6's mother's will; because of the fall in investment prices the yearly income of £1,100, is not more than £750.
Each daughter can claim an income of £250, in case of marriage, and X10 would not have much to live on.
He and X14 then travel to X15, where he scrutinizes the premises.
Within X6's room, he discovers her bed is anchored to the floor, an unconnected bell cord has been installed, and a ventilator hole connects her room to X10's.
In X10's room, they notice a large safe and a saucer of milk.
While discussing his findings with X16 remarks that X10 is comparable to Drs.
X17 and X18.
X13 instructs X6 to stay in X7's old room until X10 has retired for the night, then to show a light at the window and return to her room.
Once she has done so, X13 and X14 sneak onto the grounds and climb into X7's room.
After a tense wait, they hear a slight metallic noise and see a dim light through the ventilator, followed by a hissing sound.
X13 lights a candle and strikes at the bell cord, and they hear a terrifying scream.
X13 and X14 go to X10's room, where they see the "speckled band" – a fictional venomous swamp adder which X13 identifies as the most poisonous snake in X19.
Angered by X13's blows, the snake had attacked X10, killing him.

In order to prevent his daughters from marrying and so reducing his annual income, he had trained the snake to crawl through the ventilator and down the bell cord, bite anyone sleeping in X7's bed, and return at his whistle (using the milk as a lure).
He kept it in the safe during the day as a safety precaution.
The official inquest rules X10 met his fate while indiscreetly playing with a dangerous pet.
Though X13 also admits to indirectly killing X10, he does not foresee it troubling him and chooses not to tell the police X10's full motive to spare X6 any further grief.

title: The Adventure of the Engineer's Thumb
label: The Adventure of the Engineer's Thumb
sentences: In the summer of 1889, a young X1 and consultant hydraulic engineer, X2, is brought to X3's home one morning to receive medical attention for a severed thumb he sustained the previous night.
Once X4 has tended to the wound, he takes X5 to see X6 so the latter can hear the details of the night's events.

X5 was visited by a man who identified himself as X7 and offered to pay him 50 guineas (£, ) to examine a hydraulic press at a country house in X8 that X9 claimed was used to compress fuller's earth into bricks.
Despite his misgivings and doubts about the machine's true purpose, X5 felt compelled to accept the offer, as his business was newly established and he had little work.
Upon arriving at an appointed train station, X5 was picked up by X9 in a carriage with frosted glass windows.
They traveled what seemed to be a considerable distance, estimated by X5 to be 12 miles.
After they arrived at the house, a woman warned X5 to leave, but he disregarded her.
X9 and a man introduced as X10 took X5 to the hydraulic press.
X5 made recommendations on how to fix it, but did not believe it was being used to compress fuller's earth, as the engine was far too powerful for such a purpose.
Closer examination confirmed that the device was used to process metal.
He confronted X9, who then tried to kill him with the press.
After the woman helped X5 escape, making a reference to a "last time", a murderous X9 pursued him with a cleaver.
X5 climbed out a second-storey window and hung on to the sill, preparing to drop to the ground, but instead fell when X9 severed his thumb.
Surviving the fall, X5 passed out while fleeing among the rosebushes and later awoke by a hedge near the train station.
Once X5 finishes his story, X11 deduces that X9 and his allies are counterfeiters, and their machine was used to mint false coins.
The police confirm that a gang has been producing half crowns in large amounts, but could not be tracked until now.

From X5's account of X9's carriage horse being fresh and well-groomed, X11 concludes that the criminals are located near the station, and that the 12-mile drive with frosted glass windows was intended to disguise their location.
Checking the newspapers helps identify the "last time" the woman spoke about; a hydraulic engineer left his lodgings a year prior, and has never been seen since.
X12, and the police travel to the house X5 described, only to find it ablaze due to X5's oil lamp being crushed by the press.
Their operation ruined, the counterfeiters fled in the direction of X13, taking several large boxes that X11 believes may have held their coins.
X5 laments the loss of both his thumb and the 50 guineas, but X11 reassures him that he has gained a compelling story that he can tell for the rest of his life.

title: The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor
label: The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor
sentences: X1 comes to X2 and X3 for help after his bride, X4, disappeared during their wedding reception.
He explains that the dollar princess—heiress to a large X5 mining fortune—traveled to X6, eager to marry him after they met in X7.
However, X8 became uncharacteristically sharp with X9 following the wedding, during which she had dropped her bouquet and a gentleman in the front row returned it to her.
During the post-wedding breakfast at X9's father-in-law's home, X8 spoke with her maid before claiming "a sudden indisposition" and retired to her room.
Not long after, she is discovered to have disappeared.
Additionally, her wedding dress and ring were found washed ashore at X10 the X11 of X12 to drag the river for X8's body.
Despite X13 and X14's confusion, X15 easily deduces what happened, having dealt with similar cases before.
Upon locating X8, he forces her to reveal to X9 that the mystery man, X16.
X17, was her previous husband.
Years prior, following their own wedding, X17 had left to become a prospector.
After he was reported killed following an Apache raid on the mining camp he worked at, X8 assumed it was true and eventually met X9 even though she was still in love with X17.
Meanwhile, X17 was captured by the Apache, but escaped and followed X8 to X18 to reunite with her.
She recognised him instantly, though he gestured her to stay silent to avoid causing a scandal and secretly passed a note to her while returning her bouquet.
She subsequently faked her death to be with X17 again.
X15 convinces X8 to be more honest and apologize to X9.
However, he refuses to accept, feeling that he had been ill used.

title: The Adventure of the Beryl Coronet
label: The Adventure of the Beryl Coronet
sentences: A banker named X1 makes a loan of £50,000 to a client from one of the "highest, noblest, most exalted names in X2," implied to be a member of the British X3 and, thus, a son of X4 and an heir to the throne.
The client leaves the beryl coronet, described as one of the "most precious public possessions of the empire," as collateral.
Feeling his bank's personal safe is insufficient to protect such a rare and valuable piece of jewellery, he takes it to his home in X5 and keeps it in his dressing room.
However, he and his niece X6 later find his son X7 holding the coronet, seemingly trying to bend it, with three beryls missing from it.
A panicked X8 seeks out X9 for help.
Despite the damning evidence against X7, who refuses to give a statement, X10 is unconvinced.

With the threat of X8's reputation being besmirched and a national scandal weighing heavily on his mind, X10 determines X7 could not have broken the coronet on his own without making noise, notices footprints in the snow outside X8's home, and considers X8's servants, X6, and X7's rakish friend X11 as potential suspects.
Eventually, X10 concludes X12 is a notorious criminal who conspired with X6, unaware of his real identity, to steal the coronet.
X7 caught the pair in the act and broke the coronet while trying to take it back from X12 before taking the blame for X6 out of love for her.
Though X12 and X6 escape justice, X10 is convinced they will receive their punishment in due time.
He later buys back the missing beryls from a fence that X12 sold them to, receives compensation from X8, and tells him to apologize to X7 for assuming he was the thief.

title: The Adventure of the Copper Beeches
label: The Adventure of the Copper Beeches
sentences: X1 visits X2 for advice on whether she should accept a unique governess job with a substantial initial salary of £100 a year, on the condition that she cut her hair short, among other strange provisos.
When she initially refuses, the man who made the offer, X3, increases the offer to £120.
Despite her suspicions, X4 ultimately agrees, and leaves for X5 to work at X6's countryside estate, the X7.
X8 advises her to contact him via telegram, should she need him.
After a fortnight, X8 receives a message from X4, beseeching him to see her in X9.
After they reunite, she explains that X6 would sometimes make her wear an electric blue dress and sit in the front room, with her back to the front window.
Suspecting she was not supposed to see something outside, she used a small mirror shard hidden in her handkerchief to confirm and witnessed a man standing by the nearby road looking at the house.
Additionally, X6's wife never seemed to smile, X4's six-year-old charge was astonishingly cruel to small animals, and X4 found a cut-off tress of hair similar to her own in a locked drawer.
Furthermore, X10, a deliberately-starved and vicious Mastiff that only the drunken manservant X11 could control, was let loose every night to prowl the grounds.
As such, X4 was ordered not to cross the threshold after dark.
X4 had also been uneasy about a forbidden wing of the house where the windows were either dirty or shuttered.
At one point, X6 emerged from it, looking perturbed, and claimed he was using it as a darkroom.
Unconvinced, X4 entered the wing when X12 left his keys in the door, only to be frightened into fleeing by a moving shadow on the other side of a locked door.
She collided with X6, who attempted to comfort her and ascertain what she might have found out.
His overacting aroused X4's suspicions, confirmed when he suddenly threatened to feed her to X10 if she entered the wing again.
Accepting the case, X8 deduces someone is being held prisoner in the mystery wing.
He further deduces X6 hired X4 to impersonate his daughter X13, whom X14 was unaware of and strongly resembled, to convince the stranger outside that X13 is not interested in seeing him.
Joined by X14 and X15 breaks into the mystery wing, but it is empty.
X6 enters; deducing X13 has escaped and believing the trio helped her, he tries to sic X10 on them.
However, the dog had been starved for longer than usual and attacks its master, until X16 kills it with his revolver.
Later, X12's wife confirms X8's theory, and reveals when X13 came of age, she was to receive an annuity from her late mother's will.
X6 tried to force her to sign control of the inheritance over to him, resulting in X13 falling ill with brain fever and having her hair cut off.
He subsequently tried to keep her away from her fiancé X17 and hired X14 to maintain appearances.
It was X18 who helped X13 escape and flee with her fiancé.
Afterward, X13 marries her fiancé; X6 survives as an invalid being cared for by his second wife; and X4 becomes the principal of an all-girls' school in X19, which meets with "considerable success".

title: The Adventure of Silver Blaze
label: The Adventure of Silver Blaze
sentences: X1 and his partner, X2, travel by train to X3 to investigate a crime of disappearance of the great race horse X4 and the murder of the horse's trainer, X5.
X6 and X7 arrive at X8, from where X4 is missing.
X9 had come to X3 (and specifically to X8) to gather information about X4 and his stablemate X10.
He had approached both X11's maid and a stable boy the night of the horse's disappearance and has been arrested for the murder.
To X6, there seem to be a number of facts that do not fit the case against X12, damning as it looks.
It seems odd that he would lead the horse out on to the moor simply to injure or kill him, which could be done in his stall.
Had he stolen the animal, what good would such a famous thoroughbred be to him?
Why has an exhaustive search of the neighbourhood not turned up X4?
What has X12 done with him?
X1 soon tracks down X4; his tracks (along with a man's) are clearly visible in the soil, albeit intermittently.
X6 also deduces why the police could not find the horse, despite having looked right at him.
X6 ensures X4's safety, and turns his mind to other aspects of the case.
X13's late trainer, has been killed by a blow to the skull, assumed to have been administered by X12 with his "X14", a club-like walking stick.
X12's cravat is also found in X11's hand, and the latter's coat is found draped over a furze bush.
A knife is found at the crime scene—a peculiarly delicate-looking one, with a small blade.
X2, from his medical experience, identifies it as a cataract knife used for the most delicate surgery—useful as it is for that purpose, it would be unsuitable as a weapon.
X11 also seems to have gashed himself in the hip with it.
One of the stable lads, X15, was on guard duty the night of the crime, but he proves to have been drugged with powdered opium placed in his supper.
No one else who ate the curried mutton made at the X16's house that evening suffered any ill effects, but X17 was in a profound stupor well into the next day.
X11's pockets contained a tallow candle and a milliner's bill for (among other things) a 22-guinea dress, made out to one X18.
There is the curious incident with the dog, and a problem with the sheep kept at the stable: The boy who looks after them tells X6 that three of his animals have become suddenly lame.
X6's powers unravel the mystery and lay bare what villainies there are to be exposed.
He visits the milliners' shop in X19 and determines, using X11's photograph, that X11 posed as X20.
This establishes his motive: He had a mistress with expensive tastes and tried to rig the race to earn himself a large sum of money.
The curried mutton was a clue; only such a spicy dish could have masked the taste of powdered opium and it was impossible for X12 to arrange a highly seasoned meal that evening for his purposes.
Therefore, someone in the household must have conceived the idea, namely X11.
The "curious incident of the dog in the night-time" is easily explained: the dog made no noise because no stranger was there.
X6 explains, "I had grasped the significance of the silence of the dog, for one true inference invariably suggests others ...
Obviously, the midnight visitor was someone whom the dog knew well".
It was X11 who removed X4 from his stall and led him out onto the moor.

X11's purpose in doing this was to use the cataract knife to inflict a slight injury upon one of the horse's legs, rendering him temporarily lame in a way that would be undetectable on examination and thus likely put down to strain.
He had thought to use X12's cravat (which the latter dropped when he was expelled from X8) as a sling to hold the horse's leg to cut it.
X11 was killed when the horse, sensing that something was wrong, panicked and kicked the trainer in the head.
The lame sheep had been used by X11 for practice.
X21's main concern, of course, is getting his horse back.
X6 chooses not to tell X22 where his horse has been (although he has known all along) until after the X23, which is won by X4.
At first, the Colonel does not recognise his horse, since the animal's distinguishing white markings have been covered with dye.
The horse had been looked after by one of the Colonel's neighbours, X24, who had found him wandering the moor and hidden him in his barn.
X6 then explains the details of the case step-by-step to the satisfaction of the Colonel, X7 and X25.
X26 is one of the more competent police detectives with whom X6 works in the course of his career.

title: The Adventure of the Cardboard Box
label: The Adventure of the Cardboard Box
sentences: X1 of X2 receives a parcel in the post that contains two severed human ears packed in coarse salt.
X3 of X4 suspects a prank by three medical students whom X5 was forced to evict because of their unruly behaviour.
The parcel was sent from X6, the city of origin of one of the former boarders.
Upon examining the parcel himself, X7 is convinced that it is evidence of a serious crime.

He reasons that a medical student with access to a dissection laboratory would likely use something other than plain salt to preserve human remains, and would be able to make a more precise cut than the roughly hacked ears suggest.
The address on the package, roughly written and with a spelling correction, suggests to X7 that the sender lacks education and is unfamiliar with X2.
He further deduces that this person is a sailor, based on the particular method of tarring and knotting the string.

A few questions to X5, a few observations, a cable to X8, and an attempt to visit X5's sister X9 (thwarted by the latter's sudden illness) convince X7 that the ears belong to X5's other sister, X10, and her extramarital lover, and that they have been murdered.
He concludes that X10's estranged husband, X11, is the murderer, and that X12 had sent the ears to the X13 house in X2 (addressing it merely to "X14.
X15"), not knowing that X9 had moved away.
X12, who is an unpleasant man when drunk, had meant to horrify X9 because he ultimately blamed her for causing the trouble that led him to kill X10 and her lover.
After receiving an answer to his cable, X7 gives X16 a note and asks him not to mention X7's name in connection with the case due to its simplicity.
Two days later, he receives an envelope from X16, which contains a note stating that X12 has been arrested and a copy of his confession.
X12 is indeed a sailor, and X6 was the first port where he had the chance to post the parcel.
X16, acting on X7's information, arrested him when his ship reached X17.
According to his confession, he and X9 began to hate each other after he rejected her advances toward him.
X9 then began to plant suspicions in X10's mind concerning X12's fidelity and introduced her to another sailor, X18.

Despite X12's orders that X19 stay away from the household, he and X10 went out rowing one day; X12 followed them onto the water, killed them both, and sent an ear from each corpse to X9's old address in X2.
As X7 finishes reading X12's confession, he muses to X20, "What object is served by this circle of misery and violence and fear?"
He has no immediate answer, wondering if human reason will ever be able to find one.

title: The Adventure of the Yellow Face
label: The Adventure of the Yellow Face
sentences: X1, bored due to a want of cases, returns home from a walk with X2 early in spring to find he has missed a visitor but that the caller has left his pipe behind.

From it, X3 deduces that he was disturbed of mind (because he forgot the pipe); that he valued it highly (because he had repaired it with silver bands which cost more than the pipe cost, rather than replacing it, when it was broken); that he was muscular, left-handed, had excellent teeth, was careless in his habits (because of the tooth marks in the pipe stem and the burn patterns on the pipe bowl) and did not need to practice economy (because the pipe is packed with an expensive blend of tobacco).
None of these deductions are particularly germane to the story: they are merely X4's logical exercises.
When the visitor, X5 (whose name X3 observed from his hatband) returns, X3 and X6 hear the story of X7's deception by his wife X8.
She had been previously married in X9, but her husband and child had died of yellow fever, whereupon she returned to X10 and met and married X7.
Their marriage had been blissful until X8 asked for £100 and begged him not to ask why.
Two months later, X11 was caught conducting secret liaisons with the occupants of a cottage near the X7's house in X12.
X13 has seen a mysterious yellow-faced person in this cottage.
Overcome with jealousy, he breaks in and finds the place empty.
However, the room where he saw the mysterious figure is very comfortable and well furnished, with a portrait of his wife on the mantelpiece.
X3, after sending X7 home with instructions to wire for him if the cottage was reoccupied, confides in X6 his belief that the mysterious figure is X11's first husband.
He postulates that the husband, having been left in X9, has come to X10 to blackmail her.
After X7 summons X3 and X6, the three enter the cottage, brushing aside the entreaties of X11.
They find the strange yellow-faced character, and X3 peels the face away, showing it to be a mask, and revealing a young girl who is half-black.
It is then revealed that X11's first husband was X14, an African-American lawyer, who did die in X9, but their daughter, X15, survived.
At the time X8 came to X10, she could not bring X15 with her, as the child was still ill enough that the transition might have exacerbated her state.
But later, after she and X16 were married, X8 got word that X15 was alive and well.

Upon hearing of this, X8 became overcome with desire to see her child again, so she asked for the hundred pounds and used it to bring X15 and her nurse to X10, and installed them in the cottage near the X7's house.
She feared, however, that X16 might stop loving her if he found out that she was the mother of a mixed race child, so all the while, she had made every endeavour to keep X15's existence a secret.
Both X6 and X3 are touched by X7's response.
X6 observes: ...when X7's answer came it was one of which I love to think.
He lifted the little child, kissed her, and then, still carrying her, he held his other hand out to his wife and turned towards the door.
"We can talk about it more comfortably at home," said he.
"I am not a very good man, X8, but I think I am a better one than you have given me credit for being."

X3 excuses himself and X6, and, that evening, after they have returned to X17, says: X6, if it should ever strike you that I am getting a little overconfident in my powers, or giving less pains to a case than it deserves, kindly whisper X12 in my ear, and I shall be infinitely obliged to you.

title: The Adventure of the Stockbroker's Clerk
label: The Adventure of the Stockbroker's Clerk
sentences: A young clerk, X1, consults X2 with his suspicions concerning a company that has offered him a very well-paid job.
X3 and X4 travel by train to X5, where the job has so far been based, and X4 explains that the X6 brokerage firm at which he worked had gone out of business, leaving him unemployed.
He eventually secured a new post with another such firm in the X7, without an interview.
Before taking up the job, he was approached by X8, who offered him a better-paid managership with a newly established hardware distribution company, to be based in X9, with a £100 advance on salary.
At X10's request, X4 wrote a document accepting the position and also agreed not to send a letter of resignation to X11.
X4 was sent to X5 to meet X10's brother X12, a company co-founder.
He immediately commenced his duties, but was concerned about the unprofessional aspects of the business and its sparse offices.
Having noticed that both brothers had a gold-filled tooth at the same position in their mouths, he suspected that they might be the same man.
As the trio arrive at the office in X5, with X2 and X13 presented as fellow job-seekers, X12 goes into shock after buying and reading the evening newspaper.
He withdraws and attempts to hang himself, but X13 is able to revive him.

X2 concludes that the story of the brothers is a fabrication and that there is only one "X14," who has posed as both of them in the hope that X4 might dismiss the similarities between them as a family resemblance.

X2 further deduces that the whole point of the exercise has been to get X4 out of X6 and obtain a sample of his handwriting so that an imposter can gain employment at X11 (hence the request for X4 to not officially resign his post).
The imposter is to break into the company safe and steal the large stockpile of valuable securities kept within.
From the newspaper, they learn that X11 has suffered an attempted robbery, culminating in the murder of the weekend watchman and the capture of the thief.
Having recently completed a prison sentence, a forger/safecracker named X15 and his brother concocted the scheme to steal the securities.
X15 took the job intended for X4 so he could gain the information needed to carry out the heist, while his brother posed as both X10 and X12 to keep X4 occupied.
Bonds worth nearly £100,000 were taken, together with large amounts of scrip in mines and other companies, but the police recovered them from X15.
Sending X4 out to notify the police so they can come to arrest X15's brother, X2 comments, "Human nature is a strange mixture, X13.
You see that even a villain and murderer can inspire such affection that his brother turns to suicide when he learns that his neck is forfeited."

title: The Adventure of the Gloria Scott
label: The Adventure of the Gloria Scott
sentences: In his university days, X1 spent a month with his friend, X2, at X3's father's estate in X4.
While there, X1 amazed his host, X3's father, who was a Justice of the Peace and a landowner.
He had made his fortune in the goldfields in X5.
One of X1's deductions, that X6 was once connected to someone with the initials "X7" whom he wanted to forget, caused him to pass out on the spot.
X1 had touched a sore spot, and possibly did not believe the old man's explanation once he had come back to himself that X7 had been an old lover.
X1 perceived that he was making his host uncomfortable and decided to take his leave.
The evening before he did so, another old man named X8 suddenly appeared at the house, causing X6 to rush inside for a drink of brandy before greeting him.
They had apparently been shipmates some 30 years earlier, and X6 said something about finding him some work.
Soon afterwards, X1 and X3 found X6 drunk.
X1 then left the X9's estate and spent the next seven weeks on a set of chemistry experiments, only to receive a sudden telegram from X3 begging him to return to X4.
Once X1 arrived, X3 told him that X6 was dying as a result of a stroke suffered after he received a letter, postmarked X10 in X11.
They found that he had died while X3 had been meeting X1 at the station.
After X1's earlier departure, X8 proved to be as unruly an employee as could be imagined.
He had demanded to be promoted from gardener to butler and had got what he wanted.
He was often drunk, and took extensive liberties with the property and servants which would normally have resulted in an employee's dismissal.
Despite X3's disapproval and the other servants' complaints, X6 continued to let X8 do as he pleased.
Suddenly, X8 announced that he was leaving because he had tired of X4, and he was going to X11 to see X12, another old shipmate.
X8's presence had caused great stress to X3, who thought the trouble would end once X8 left.
The arrival of the letter proved him wrong, however.
It read: "The supply of game for X13 is going steadily up.
Head-keeper X8, we believe, has been now told to receive all orders for fly-paper and for preservation of your hen pheasant's life."
The letter meant nothing to X3, but X1 eventually realised that it contained a hidden message based on reading the first word and every third one thereafter: "The game is up.
X8 has told all.
Fly for your life."
X1 concluded that the "game" was a blackmail scheme perpetrated by X8 against both X12 and X6.
The latter's dying words to his doctor led X3 to some papers hidden in a cabinet, which contained a full account of X6's past.
Born X14, he had been convicted of embezzling money from the bank where he worked.
He was sentenced to transportation and put aboard a ship, the X15, bound for X5 from X16.
One of X17's fellow prisoners, X18, told him of a conspiracy to take over the ship.
X19 had bribed most of the ship's crew and officers, and had arranged for a confederate posing as a chaplain to smuggle weapons and equipment to the prisoners.
The takeover began ahead of schedule when the doctor discovered a prisoner's weapons while treating him.
The others stormed the deck, killing the captain and many other men while suffering heavy losses, but a dispute soon arose over what to do with the survivors who had not been privy to the plot.
Those who wanted to spare the men's lives, including X17 and a prisoner named X20, were given a boat and supplies and allowed to leave.

Shortly afterward, the X15 was destroyed when a barrel of gunpowder exploded in the violence that continued aboard after their departure, and they found X8 alive amid the wreckage and took him onto the boat.
Picked up by another X21 ship the following day, the men on the boat passed themselves off as shipwreck survivors.
X17 and X20 respectively assumed new identities as X9 and X12 upon reaching X22 and began to work in the goldfields.
Both of them later returned to X23 as wealthy men and lived comfortably until X8 tracked them down and threatened to expose their criminal pasts.
Heartbroken by his father's death, X3 traveled to the X24 and began to work at its tea plantations.
Since no scandal involving the X15 was ever reported after X12's letter arrived, and since neither X8 nor X12 was ever heard from again, the police believed X8 had murdered X12 and fled.
X1 concluded the opposite: that X12 had killed X8, mistakenly assuming that he had told the secret, and then left X23 with whatever money he had at hand.

title: The Adventure of the Musgrave Ritual
label: The Adventure of the Musgrave Ritual
sentences: In a frame story, X1 goes through some of his old records, and recounts one of his earliest cases to X2.
Former university acquaintance, X3, calls on X1 regarding strange events at X4, his ancient family manor house.

X5 have dwelt at X4 since before the English Civil War; since that time period, each eldest son of the house memorizes and recites a strange poem upon coming of age: Late one night, X6 unable to sleep, hears a noise.
Investigating, he catches his longtime butler, X7, secretly studying the ritual and other private papers.
Angered by this inappropriate behavior, X6 orders X7 to immediately leave the premises.
X7 begs for time to appear that he left of his own accord to avoid public disgrace.
X6 grants him a week, but a few days later, X7 disappears, leaving behind all his belongings.
His bed has not been slept in, and no one saw him leave.
A maid, X8 had spurned for another woman—becomes hysterical when questioned and is confined to a sickbed, still raving.
A hired nurse watches over her, but X9 escapes during the night.
Following X9's trail, X6 and the police discover a satchel she threw into the manor lake that contains nothing but twisted metal and a few mud-covered coloured stones.
Like X10 realises that the seemingly meaningless ritual was likely instructions to a valuable object's hiding place.
Ascertaining the height of the biggest oak tree on the property, and the location of a former giant elm tree, X1 repeats X7's actions, which lead into an abandoned wing of the house.
The cellar under this wing is used for storing lumber; X1 finds the wood pushed to one side, revealing a metal ring in one of the floor stones with X7's muffler tied to it.
With help from X6 and a policeman, X1 raises the heavy stone to reveal a deep hole in the floor.
Below is X7's asphyxiated body lying across an ancient wooden chest.
A few coins from the X11's era are scattered inside the hole.
After the body is removed, X1 notices several wood billets that were likely used as levers or props to raise the stone.
X1 deduces that X12 to lift the heavy stone alone—recruited X9 to help lift the stone, using the wood pieces.
After X7 climbed in and handed the satchel up to X9, the slab fell shut, either accident or intentionally, with X9 fleeing out of guilt.
X1 cleans and examines the satchel's contents, revealing that the metal pieces are gold and the stones gems.
The fragments are the remains of X13, which belonged to X11 ("He who is gone").
X14 confirms that his ancestor, X15, was a high-ranking X16 close to X11's son and heir, X17 ("He who will come").
X18 was likely given the crown for safekeeping, and hid it beneath the stone and created the ritual as a clue to its location.
The ritual's meaning was never passed down before X18 died; for the next 200 years, the poem was considered a quaint family custom.
After much legal and governmental interactions, the X5 are allowed to keep the fragments on display.
X9 is never found, and X6 fears she has committed suicide, though X1 believes it more likely that she fled the country.

title: The Adventure of the Reigate Squire
label: The Adventure of the Reigate Squire
sentences: X1 takes X2 to a friend's estate near X3 in X4 to rest after a rather strenuous case in X5.
Their host is X6, who tells them of a recent burglary at the nearby X7's estate in which the thieves stole a motley assortment of things with little or no value.
The next morning, the Colonel's butler brings news of a murder at another nearby estate, the X8.
The victim is X9, the coachman.

X10 has taken charge of the investigation, and there is one physical clue: a torn piece of paper found in X11's hand with a few words written on it, including "quarter to twelve", which was approximately the time of X11's murder.
X2 takes an instant interest in the note.
One of the first facts to emerge is that there is a longstanding legal dispute between the X12 and the X8.
X2 interviews the two X13 men, X14 young X15 and his ageing father.
X15 tells X2 that he saw the burglar struggling with X11 when a shot went off and X11 fell dead, and that the burglar ran off through a hedge to the road.
The elder X13 claims that he was in his room smoking at the time, and X15 says that he had also still been up.
A door had been forced open, but according to X15's account, X11 and the burglar had struggled outside the house.
X2 theorises that the murderer snatched the note because it could incriminate him/her, but did not realise that a scrap of it remained in X11's hand.
X11's mother proves to be no help due to her old age, deafness, and lack of intelligence.
X2, apparently still recovering from his previous strenuous case, seems to have a fit just as X16 is about to mention the note to the X8.
Afterward, X2 remarks that it is extraordinary that a burglar would break into the X8 house when the X8 were both still awake and had lamps lit.
X2 then apparently makes a mistake writing an advertisement that the elder X13 corrects.
X2 insists on searching the X8 rooms despite their protests that the burglar could not have gone there.
He sees X15's room and then his father's, where he deliberately knocks a small table over, sending some oranges and a water carafe to the floor.
The others were not looking his way at the time, and X2 implies that the cause is X1's clumsiness.
X1 plays along and starts gathering up the scattered fruit.
Everyone then notices that X2 has left the elder X13's room, and father and son both rush out in search of him.
Moments later, X2 is heard calling for help from X15's room, where X1 and X16 find X15 trying to strangle X2 and the father twisting his wrist.
Both are quickly restrained, and X2 advises X16 to arrest them for X11's murder.
The guilty looks on their faces, and X15's attempt to draw a revolver, convince X16 that X2's accusation is valid.
X2 had found the remainder of the note in the pocket of X15's dressing-gown.

It ran thus (the words in boldface are the ones on the original scrap): "If you will only come round at quarter to twelve to the east gate you will learn what will very much surprise you and maybe be of the greatest service to you and also to X17.
But say nothing to anyone upon the matter."
X2, an expert at studying handwriting, reveals that he had realised earlier from the torn piece of paper that the note was written by two men, each writing alternate words.
He had perceived that one man was young, the other rather older, and that they were related, which led X2 to conclude that the X8 wrote the note.
X2 saw that the X8 story was false since X11's body has no powder burns on it, so he was not shot at point-blank range as the X8 claim.
The escape route also does not bear their story out: there is a boggy ditch next to the road that the fleeing murderer would have had to cross, yet there are no signs of any footprints in it.

X2 had faked his fit to prevent the X8 from being reminded about and destroying the missing part of the note, and made a mistake in the advertisement on purpose to get the elder X13 to write the word "twelve" by hand, to compare it with the note fragment.
The elder X13's confidence is broken after his arrest and he tells all.
X2 had already deduced that he and his son were responsible for the X7's burglary; they had broken in to search for documents supporting X18's legal claim against them, but found none.
X11 had apparently learned of the crime and decided to blackmail them, not realising that it was dangerous to do such a thing to X15.
The X8 wrote the note as bait to trap X11, using the recent burglary scare as a plausible way to explain his death.
X2 remarks that they might have succeeded if they had recovered the entire note and paid more attention to detail.

title: The Adventure of the Crooked Man
label: The Adventure of the Crooked Man
sentences: X1 calls upon X2 at his surgery late one night to request his assistance in an investigation.
X1 explains that, in X3 of X4 (in some editions X5) and his wife X6 were a seemingly happy couple; however, X7 has died, and his wife is suspected of his murder.
X8's contact in the regiment, has explained that X7, while completely devoted to his wife, had a rather vindictive nature elsewhere.
He had also been subject to random fits of depression, and disliked being left alone at night.
The night of the supposed crime, X9 left for a church meeting in company with her friend, X10.
When she returned, she was considerably agitated and asked her maid for tea.
When the maid returned with the tea, she overheard the X11 furiously arguing behind the locked morning room door.
X12, the only one loud enough to be clearly audible, repeatedly said the words "X13", "coward", and "give me back my life".
Moments later, screams rang out; when the X7's coachman entered the room through the open French windows, he found X12 collapsed and the colonel dead, bleeding from a head wound.
The key to the room was missing, and the door had to be opened by a locksmith.
X12, temporarily insane from shock, was removed to a hospital, and X1 was called in to investigate.
X1 finds signs that a silent third party had been present; the man had left his stick in the room, his footprints in the lawn, and presumably also had taken the key.
X1 also finds the pawmarks of a short-legged, long-bodied animal on the floor, as well as signs the creature had attempted to eat the X7's pet canary.
Interrogating X14 learns that, on the way home from the meeting, she and X12 had encountered a deformed man with a wooden box on his back.
Both he and X12 seemed badly startled; he addressed her by name, and she called him "X15".
They spoke privately for a moment, then parted, both very upset.
After swearing her friend to silence, X12 returned home.
As the man's appearance was distinctive, X1 was soon able to discover his identity: X16, a conjurer who entertained the soldiers around X17.
With X2 as a witness, X1 visits X18 in his lodgings.
X18 gladly tells his story to save X12 from being accused of murder.
Thirty years prior, he had been in X19, a soldier in the X20 with X21.
Both men loved X22, but she was devoted to X18, despite her father's disapproval.
The couple remained true to each other, nonetheless, but when the Indian Rebellion of 1857 erupted, the X20 found themselves cut off from supplies.

X18 volunteered to go for help, and X7 gave him information on how to safely sneak through the enemy lines; however, X7, wishing to have X12 to himself, secretly alerted the insurgents that X18 would be passing.
X18 was captured, and learned from his captors of the betrayal.
Over the years, he was repeatedly enslaved and tortured, resulting in his deformed back and legs.
Finally escaping, he lived for many years in X19 as a conjurer, preferring X12 and his fellow soldiers to think he had been killed in action instead of seeing his deformity.
In his old age, wanting to see X23 and be around soldiers again, he saved enough money to travel to X17, not realizing his own old regiment was currently stationed there.
Unexpectedly running into X12, he had admitted her husband's betrayal to her, then secretly followed her to her house.

Seeing X7 arguing with X24 had entered the room through the French windows to defend her, but X7 had instantly died of apoplexy at the mere sight of X18 alive and struck his head on the fender as he fell.
X12 screamed and fainted.
In the chaos, X18's pet mongoose X25 escaped his wooden box, and ran up the curtain after the canary.
Reflexively pocketing the door key, X18 recaptured X25 and fled the scene, afraid he would be accused of murder.
Like X26 is hesitant to rake up a 30-year-old military scandal; learning that the medical examiner has confirmed the colonel died of apoplexy, X1 keeps X18's story secret for the time being.

Questioned by X2 about X12's use of the name "X13" when no one involved in the case went by that name, X1 decides that X12 must have been comparing her husband to the X27, who arranged the murder of X28 to have X28's wife X29.

title: The Adventure of the Resident Patient
label: The Adventure of the Resident Patient
sentences: X1 and X2 are consulted by X3, a young general practitioner whose specialty is neurological disorders.
Two years prior, having been a brilliant student but lacking the money to set up in practice, X4 agreed to a strange business proposition put forward by X5.
X6 bought a house in X7, furnished it, paid servants, and purchased everything X8 could need; All X4 had to do was set up a consulting room.
Each evening, X6 would check the day's accounts and take three-quarters of the doctor's earnings, put it in his strong box, and leave the remainder for the doctor.
Another unusual condition is having X6 to live in the house as a permanent resident patient due to his heart trouble.
The investment has made X6 rich, and X4 has become a well-known, respected doctor.

However, some months ago, X6 panicked after claiming to have read a newspaper article about a nearby burglary; he insisted upon stronger locks and other stringent security measures, and also refused to leave the house for several weeks, only recently resuming his habit of taking his evening walk.
Secondly, the evening before X4's visit to X1, an elderly Russian nobleman and his son consulted the doctor, due to the father's complaint of catalepsy.
The son remained in the waiting room while the father spoke to the doctor – however, the old gentleman suffered a cataleptic attack while in the consulting room.
X9 spent several minutes looking for some amyl nitrite, but both father and son were gone when he returned with it.
They visited again the next evening, apologizing for mistakenly believing the consultation was over the day before.
X9 again consulted the father while the son waited outside.
After the pair left, X6 returned from his walk, found footprints in his room, and entered into a state of panic again, insisting X4 go and fetch X1 to his aid.
X1 and X2 return to X7 with the doctor, but X6 refuses to admit to X1 why he is obviously afraid for his life, or why there are men pursuing him.
He instead pretends that he believes they are unknown burglars, who are after the fortune he keeps in the chest at the foot of his bed (which he does since he does not trust bankers).
X1 eventually leaves in disgust, advising X6 that he cannot help him unless he tells the truth.
However, by studying the footprints, X1 has been able to confirm the doctor's story and eliminate him as a suspect.

It was the nobleman's son who twice entered the room, first while his father (most likely) pretended to have a cataleptic seizure the day before, then a second time while the doctor was kept busy consulting the father, leaving wet footprints since it was rather rainy outside the second day.
However, X6 had been out walking both times, inadvertently frustrating his enemies.
The next morning, X1 and X2 return to X7 at a summons from X4.
X6 has been found dead, having apparently hanged himself during the night.
X1 and X10 of X11 examine the scene; X1 is able to find convincing evidence (different brands of cigars/ash, footprints, tools left behind) that three intruders were in the house that night.
Two of them are the supposed "Russian nobleman" and his son; the third is unknown.
Signs indicate the trio were admitted into the house by a confederate, most likely the newly hired page.
They then held a sort of mock-judicial proceeding against X6, "condemned" him, hanged him, and retreated, the confederate barring the door behind them.
Taking a photograph of X12 leaves to consult X11 files, and returns with the news that he has identified X6 as X13, one of the five members of the X14.
The others were X15, and X16.
After the gang committed a massive robbery in 1875 where the bank's caretaker was killed, X13 turned his four comrades in to the police in exchange for leniency.
X17 was hanged for murdering the caretaker, and the other three got lengthy prison terms of 15 years apiece.
To hide from them, X13 changed his name to X6 and moved in with X8.
However, X13's comrades qualified for parole several years before their term was up; his first panic was when he read of their unexpected early release from prison.
As he feared, they eventually hunted him down and murdered him to avenge X17.
X13 was unable to tell X1 the truth of the matter because he would have had to reveal his true identity, which, given the circumstances, he was too frightened and ashamed to do.
X18 arrests the page and instigates a search, but X19, and X16 escape the country.
The case against the page breaks down for lack of evidence, and the three murderers are suspected to have died in the wreck of the X20, off the Portuguese coast.

title: The Adventure of the Greek Interpreter
label: The Adventure of the Greek Interpreter
sentences: One summer evening, while engaged in an aimless conversation that has come round to the topic of hereditary attributes, X1 learns that X2, far from being a one-off in his powers of observation and deductive reasoning, in fact has an elder brother whose skills X3 claims outstrip even his own.
As a consequence of this, X4 becomes acquainted with the X5 and his friend's brother, X6.

X6, as X4 learns, does not have the energy of his younger brother and as a consequence is uninterested in using his great skills for detective work: In spite of his inertia, the X7 has often delivered the correct answer to a problem that X8 has brought to him.
On this occasion, however, it is X6 who has need to consult X8.
X9, a Greek interpreter and neighbour of X6, tells of a rather unnerving experience he has recently gone through.
X10 was called upon one evening by a X11, to go to a house, supposedly in X12, to translate on a business matter.
On the way there in X13's coach, X10 noticed that the windows were papered over so that he could not see where he was.
X13 also produced a bludgeon, laying it beside him as an implied threat.
X10 protested, saying that what X13 was doing was unlawful.
The kidnapper replied that he would make it up to X10, but threatened him with unspecified retribution should the evening's business ever be made public.
For approximately two hours they drove, at last arriving at a house.
It was dark, and X10 got only a general impression of a large property as he was hustled out of the coach and into the house.
The house itself was poorly lit, but X10 made out that it was quite big.

In the room into which he was led by X13 and another, nervous, giggling gentleman—whose name is later discovered to be X14 noticed a deep-pile carpet, a high marble mantel, and a suit of Japanese armour.
Another man was brought into the room.
He was thin and emaciated and had sticking plaster all over his face, and a bandage sealing his mouth.
X10 was sly enough to observe that his kidnappers were utterly ignorant of Greek, and used this to find out some information.
While X13 and his companion had X10 translate demands that the man sign some papers, X10 added his own short questions to the dialogue.

The man not only answered X13 that he would never sign these papers, but he also answered X10 that his name was X15, that he had been in X16 for three weeks, that he had no idea what house he was in, and that his captors at the house were starving him.
He wrote all his answers, unable as he was to speak through the sticking plaster.
Much could be inferred from X15's answers to X13, too.
Evidently, X13 was trying to coerce X15 into signing over property to him, and a woman was also involved.
X13 had warned X15 that his obstinacy would do her no good.
X10 would have extracted the whole story from the stranger had the woman herself not burst in unexpectedly, but even that event furnished new information.
She recognised X15 as "X17", whereupon he managed to get the bandage off his mouth and he called her "X18".
They both behaved as though neither had expected to see the other.
X10 was ushered back into the coach for another interminable ride and was deposited far from his home on X19.
He made it to X20 just in time for the last train to X21.
He had presented his story at the X5 to X6, who asks his brother X8 to look into it.
An advertisement has been placed begging the public for information.
It yields a result.
A X22 knows the woman in question, and she is currently residing at X23, a house in X24.
X2 and his brother X6, who received the message from X25, decide that they must go to X24 to see about this.
X4 comes, too, and they decide to pick up X26, and X10 as well in case some translating needs to be done.
They find, however, that he has already been picked up, by a nervous, giggling man brandishing a bludgeon.
X3 knows that this means the thugs know that X10 has betrayed them.
After the necessary legal procedures for securing a search warrant have been completed, the group proceeds to X24 only to discover that the house has been abandoned.
Tracks indicate that a fully loaded coach has recently pulled out of the drive.
Breaking in, they discover X10 and X15 bound in a closed room where some charcoal has been lit to gas the two of them: X10 recovers thanks to X4's timely intervention, but X15 is already dead.
Apparently, X15 never signed any papers.

title: The Adventure of the Naval Treaty
label: The Adventure of the Naval Treaty
sentences: X1, a young X2 employee from X3, sends a letter to X4, a former schoolfellow of his.
X5 indicates something has caused him a nine-week attack of brain fever; now that he has recovered, he begs X6 to bring X7 to his aid.
X7 views the letter, and deduces that it was dictated to, and written by, a woman.
He accompanies X6 to X8's house.
There, they are greeted by X9, the brother of X10 (the writer of the letter).
X11 shows them in to see X5, who is still recovering from his long illness and being nursed by X12.
X5 lays the case before X7.
Two months earlier, his uncle and superior in the X13, had ordered him to copy an important naval treaty between X14 and X15.
The treaty was to be kept secret, for many foreign governments would want to read it.
X5 told no one of this assignment, and waited until the building was empty except for X16, the commissionaire, and his wife, who did the charring.
X5 then copied the papers as quickly as he could but it soon became apparent the task would take most of the night.
X5 rang the bell for some coffee.
X17 took the order to her husband; much later, X5 came downstairs to investigate why he had not received his coffee and found X16 had fallen asleep.
The bell to X5's office rang; realizing someone was in the room, X5 dashed back upstairs and found the naval treaty gone.
There were no hiding places, and no one could have passed X5 on the front stair, so the thief must have come and gone by the back stair.
X5, a constable, and X18 of X19 frantically searched for the thief without success.
X5 had a nervous breakdown and was escorted back to X20.
As X11's bedroom was best suited for a sickroom, X11 was forced out of it by the doctor.
X21 has remained there, nursed by X12 by day and a hired nurse by night.
X7 starts the investigation at the X2, interviewing both X22 and X18.
He learns that the X23 and a X24, were suspected and then cleared.
X22 informs him that no foreign government has received the treaty yet, which seems odd since nine weeks have passed.
X7 also discovers that X12 and X11 were never meant to be long-term guests; they had come down for a few days' visit when the tragedy occurred but had stayed so X12 could nurse her fiancée.
Returning to X20 the next day, X7 learns that X5 dispensed with the hired nurse the evening before.
Later that same evening, someone tried to break into X5's sickroom window with a knife.
X5 immediately roused the household, but the burglar got away.
Unbeknownst to X5 or X25 orders X12 to stay in the sickroom until bedtime and to lock the door behind her when she leaves.
He then arranges that X5 and X6 should go to X26.
X6 takes X5 back to X27, but neither can understand X7's actions.
The next morning, X7 arrives with disheveled clothes and a bandaged hand.
At the breakfast table, he pretends to have found nothing, but then arranges for X28 to serve X5 the treaty on his breakfast plate.
X5 is overjoyed to have it back, nearly fainting with relief.
X7 had realized X9 was responsible.
The sickroom was formerly his bedroom, and only someone in the house could have known when no nurse would be on guard.
X11 had come to X21's office to ask if X21 was coming home, rung the bell, then found the treaty.
As X11 had some stock exchange debts to pay, he stole the treaty, intending to sell it, and hid it under the floorboards of his bedroom.
However, X21's breakdown and the two nurses on hand in the room had kept X11 from getting at the treaty for weeks.
The first chance he had, X11 had tried and failed to steal the treaty back.
X7 had kept X12 in the room so X11 could not get at the treaty during the daytime.
After she left, X11 broke in and retrieved the treaty, but X7 ambushed him, and boxed him for the papers.

title: The Final Problem
label: The Final Problem
sentences: An injured X1 arrives at X2's residence one evening, having escaped three separate murder attempts that day.
X1 reveals to X2 he has been tracking X3 and his organisation for months, who are responsible for most of the crimes orchestrated in X4.
As X1 is close to snaring them all and delivering them to the police, X3 visits X1 at X5 earlier that day and warns him to withdraw from his pursuit of justice against him.
X1 admits that X3 could thwart his plans given his great mind that could rival his, and plans to flee to X6 while the police capture X3 and his gang.
X1 invites X2 to join him on the trip.

X1 then gives him unusual instructions intended to hide his tracks to the boat train at X7 station before leaving X2's house by climbing over the back wall in the garden, paranoid that he might be followed.
The next day, X2 follows X1's instructions and finds himself waiting in the reserved first-class coach for his friend, who is disguised as an elderly Italian priest.
X1 informs X2 that the rooms at X8 had been set on fire the previous night, in an unsuccessful attempt to both kill him and destroy the evidence he had collected against X3.
As the boat train pulls out of X9 spots X3 on the platform trying to stop the train.
X1 deduces that X3 has tracked X2 despite extraordinary precautions.
Changing their planned route, X1 and X2 alight at X10, hiding behind the luggage as X3 (who had chartered a special one-coach train) passes them in pursuit.

After X1 and X2 have crossed the X11 and made their way to X12 via X13 receives a message from the X4 police that most of X3's gang have been arrested in X14, but X3 has escaped and is in pursuit of X15.
He urges X2 to return to X14 as he considers himself a very dangerous companion, but X2 chooses to stay with him.
The two continue to X16 and visit the X17.
At the X18, a boy hands X2 a letter, saying that there is a dying Englishwoman at the hotel who seeks an English doctor.
X1 sends X2 back to tend to her and remains at the X18.
Upon reaching the hotel, X2 discovers that he has been tricked and rushes back to aid X1.

At the X18, he only finds two sets of footprints that lead to the end of the path, where he uncovers other signs of a violent struggle and a note from X1 explaining that he knew of the hoax but chose to fight X3 himself.

title: The Adventure of the Norwood Builder

sentences: X1 and X2 are visited by X3, a young lawyer from X4 who has been accused of murdering one of his clients – X5.

title: The Adventure of the Dancing Men

title: The Adventure of the Solitary Cyclist

sentences: X1 is contacted by X2 of X3 about an unusual turn in her and her mother's lives.

There was an ad in the news asking about their whereabouts.
Answering it, they met X5 and X6, the former a pleasant enough man, but the latter a bullying churl.

X10 began by offering X4 a job as a live-in music teacher for his ten-year-old daughter at £100 a year, about twice the going rate.
She accepted after X10 said that she could visit her mother on weekends.
That went well until X6 came to stay for a week.
He made the most oafish advances to her, and boasted that if X4 married him she would have a life of luxury.
He even grabbed her and demanded a kiss, precipitating expulsion by his host, X10.

The specific thing that has brought X4 to seek X1's services, however, is the strange man who follows her on his bicycle as she cycles to and from the railway station for her weekend visits to her mother.
The strange man always keeps his distance behind her and disappears without a trace, never letting her near him, and always along the same lonely stretch of road.
X4 does not recognise him, but he has a black beard.
X1 asks her about her admirers, and other than X11, if he can be styled as such, she can only think of X5, who, although a perfect gentleman at all times, seems attracted to her.
After X4 leaves, X1 observes that it is odd that a household would pay £100 a year for a music teacher but be too cheap to pay for a horse and trap.

This turns out to be virtually nothing, except to establish that the lady's story is true, and that the mystery man comes out of and goes back into a local house, X15.
X1 upbraids X16 for his lackluster results.
They also receive a letter from X4 the next day saying that X10 has proposed to her, but she had to refuse since she is already engaged to a X17, an electrical engineer in X18.

The innkeeper merely mentioned that X11 is a regular weekend guest at X15, which is rented by X19, who, rumour has it, is a clergyman.
X1 returns to X20 with his face somewhat marred, and another letter arrives from X4, saying that her situation has become impossible owing to X5's proposals, and X6's reappearance.
She is quitting.
X1 knows that some intrigue is afoot, and he tells X16 that they must get themselves to X14 to see that X4 makes it to the station.

Failing to realise that X4 might take an earlier train than usual, X1 discovers that he is too late to meet X4.

They come face-to-face with the mysterious cyclist, who pulls a revolver on them; however, both parties quickly realise that they are on the same side – both have X4's welfare in mind.

He evidently knows something of the intrigue.

X11's boast of having married X4 leads the mysterious cyclist, unmasking himself as X10, to pull out his revolver and shoot X11, wounding him.

title: The Adventure of the Priory School
label: The Adventure of the Priory School
sentences: X1 receives a visit from X2, the founder and principal of a preparatory school called X3 in X4.
He beseeches X1 to come back to X5 with him to look into the disappearance of one of his pupils, the ten-year-old X6, whose father is the very rich and famous X7.
X8 explains that not only the boy has disappeared, but also the German master, X9, along with his bicycle.
Once in the X10, the Duke says to X1 that he does not think that his estranged wife has anything to do with his son's disappearance, nor has there been a ransom demand.
X1 establishes that the boy and his kidnappers could not have used the nearby road without being seen, suggesting that they went cross-country.
As if to confirm this, the police find the boy's school cap in some gypsies' possession.
They swear that they simply found it on the moor, but the police lock them up.

They find a bicycle track, but it is not X9's; it does not match his tyres.

After that, X1 and X12 arrive at the X13, and meet the innkeeper, X14, who seems startled indeed to hear that X1 wants to go to X15, the Duke's nearby house, to tell him news of his son.
The two men have lunch there, and X1 suddenly realises that he and X12 saw many cow tracks out on the moor, but never at any time did they see any cows.
Furthermore, the patterns of the hoof prints were quite unusual, suggesting that the cow in question trotted, cantered, and galloped.
X1 and X12 sneak out to X16's stable and examine the horse's hooves.
As X1 has expected, there is evidence of recent shoeing, but with old shoes and new nails.
Examining the nearby smithy, X1 and X12 are rather belligerently asked to leave by X17.
Shortly afterwards, the two men hide as a cyclist comes along the road from the direction of the Duke's.
It is X18, the Duke's personal secretary, and he looks agitated.
He arrives at the inn.
Soon afterwards, a trap pulls out of the stable yard and goes along the road towards X19.
A while later, someone else – it is getting dark and only a fleeting glimpse of the new visitor is caught – arrives at the inn.
Coming closer, X1 observes X20's bicycle tyres and notes that they are the same make as the first ones encountered on the moor.
The next morning, they go to X15, where they find that the Duke is not well.
Nevertheless, X1 demands from him a cheque for £6000, saying that he has earned the reward.
His son is at the X21, and the accused is the Duke himself, but the actual mastermind of this crime is X18, who has a terrible secret: He is the illegitimate son of the Duke.
He conceived a plan to kidnap X6 to force the Duke to change his will, knowing very well that his father would not call the police on him, as he abhorred the very idea of scandal.
The plan had begun to unravel when X20 hired X16 – who has now fled, but been caught on X1's information – to do the actual kidnapping.
X16 had killed X9, and when X20 heard the news, he confessed all to his father.
So anxious had been the Duke to avoid scandal, he agreed to let his younger son remain confined at the inn for another three days, and to keep quiet, so that X16 could flee justice.
All ends well, except for X16, who faces the gallows.
X6 is brought home from the inn and the Duke writes to his estranged wife asking her to reconcile with him.
This he feels she will be willing to do, for the source of the friction between them is going away: X18 is being packed off to X22 to seek his fortune.

The shoes were from the Duke's collection of family memorabilia.
The story ends with X1 receiving the £6000 reward from the Duke for his services, joking "I am a poor man".
The next story, "X23 of X24", confirms that such a large payment is very unusual for X1.

title: The Adventure of Black Peter

sentences: X1 in the X2 is the scene of a harpoon murder, and a young police inspector, X3, asks X4, whom he admires, for help.
X4 has already determined that it would take a great deal of strength and skill to run a man through with a harpoon and embed it in the wall behind him.

X7 did not sleep in the family house, but in a small hut that he built some distance from the house, whose interior he had decorated to look like a sailor's cabin on a ship.

X8 could find no footprints or other physical evidence.
However, a tobacco pouch made of sealskin and with X9 the X10's was found at the scene, full of strong ship's tobacco.
This is rather unusual, as X11" as people called him—seldom smoked.

X7 was found fully dressed, suggesting that he was expecting a visitor, and there was some rum laid out along with two dirty glasses.
There were brandy and whisky, too, but neither had been touched.
There was also a knife in its sheath at X7's feet; X12 has identified it as her husband's.
A little notebook was also found at the scene.
It contains X13.
X14 and the year 1883.
X15 on the second page, which X4 reckons stands for X16.
The first set of initials is likely a stockbroker's, as the little book is full of what appears to be stock exchange information.
X4 decides to accompany X8 to X1 and, upon arrival, X8 observes that someone has recently tried to break into X7's cabin, but failed.
After examining the inside of the cabin, X4 deduces from the lack of dust that something has been taken from a shelf, even though the burglar did not get in.
