X4 believes that the burglar will likely try again, this time bringing a more useful tool for the job.
So, X17, and X8 all lie in wait for the burglar that night, and they are not disappointed.
Along he comes, m breaks into the cabin, and goes through one of X7's old logbooks, cursing when he finds that the information that he wants is missing, having been torn out of the book.
As he is leaving the cabin, X8 moves in and arrests him.
He is X18 matches the initials in the notebook—the son of a long-vanished, failed banker.
He claims he was looking at X7's logs to test a theory of his.
His father disappeared with a box full of securities after his bank failed.
He took them on a yacht bound for X19.
He believes that his father's boat may have been driven north in the X20 by bad weather, and met the X21, captained by X7.

He believes that X7 knew something about his father's disappearance, and that possibly his father was murdered by the man who has now himself become a murder victim as he has traced some of his father's long lost securities back to X7.
X8 takes X22 off to the station, even though X22 swears that he has nothing to do with the murder.
X4 believes this to be true, because X22 is a slight, anaemic thin man, hardly capable of running a man through with a harpoon.
X4 saves X22 from the noose by finding the true killer in a most unusual way.
He advertises for a harpooner, posing as a sea captain X23.
He gets three applicants at X24 for the job, and one of them is indeed X5's killer, as confirmed by his name, X25, and the fact that X4 had established that he was once X7's shipmate.
X4 also felt sure that a murderer would want to leave the country for a while.
X4 handcuffs the unaware X26 after which X26 confesses.
While he freely admits to killing X7, he furiously denies that it was murder, claiming self-defence.
He was actually at X7's cabin to extort hush money from him.

X22's father had indeed come aboard the X21 with his tin box of securities, and X7 had murdered him by throwing him overboard while he believed no-one was looking, though X26 had secretly witnessed the event.

title: The Adventure of Charles Augustus Milverton
label: The Adventure of Charles Augustus Milverton
sentences: X1 is hired by the X2, to retrieve compromising letters from a blackmailer: X3, who causes X1 more revulsion than any of the 50-odd murderers in his career.
X3 is "the king of blackmailers".
He demands £7,000 (£763,572 in 2025) for the letters, which if given to third parties would cause a scandal that would end X4's marriage engagement.
X1 offers £2,000, all X4 can pay, but X3 insists on £7,000.

It is worth £7,000 to him, he explains, to make an example of X4; it is in his long-term interest to ensure that his future blackmail victims would be more "open to reason" and pay him what he wants, knowing he will destroy them if they do not.
X1 resolves to recover the letters by whatever means necessary, as X3 has placed himself outside the bounds of morality.
X1 visits X5 house, disguised as a plumber, in order to learn the plan of the house and X3's daily routine.
He cultivates the acquaintance of X3's housemaid and even becomes engaged to marry her.
This rather shocks X6, but X1 assures him that he has a hated rival who will step in when the plumber disappears.
X1 has learned where X3 keeps his blackmail papers (a safe in his study), and plans to burgle X3's house that night.
X6 comes along.
They break into the study, but just as X1 opens the safe, X3 enters the study, even though he should be in bed asleep.
X1 and X6 hide behind a curtain, while X3 has a midnight meeting with a supposed maidservant offering to sell letters that would compromise her mistress.
The woman is actually one of X3's former victims, whose broken-hearted husband died when she wouldn't pay X3 and he revealed her secret.
Now she avenges her husband by shooting X3 to death, then stamps on his face.
X6 instinctively begins to rush out and stop the shooting, but X1 restrains him.
X1 understands, and X6 instantly realises, "that it was no affair of ours; that justice had overtaken a villain..."
The woman runs away, and X3's household is roused by the shots.
During his final confrontation, X3's entire cache of blackmail papers had been in a safe with its door slightly ajar.
X1 now feeds this mass of compromising material into X3's burning fireplace, despite the risk of being discovered and caught.
Then X1 and X6 escape through the garden and over the wall.
X6 has to kick himself free from a pursuer who has grabbed his leg.
The next morning, X7 calls at X8 to ask for X1's help in investigating X3's murder, which he ascribes to the two burglars seen escaping over the garden wall.
He has a description of one of them: "a middle-aged, strongly built man-square jaw, thick neck, moustache..."
X1 calls the description vague, and even jokes that it could describe X6, which amuses X9.
But X1 refuses X9's request, stating that he sympathizes with the criminals rather than the victim.
Later, X1 recognises the face of the woman who killed X3.
He shows X6 her photograph displayed in a shop-window among those of other celebrities.
X6 recognises the name of her famous husband, but X1 signals silence with a finger to his lips.
X6 assures his readers that the killer in question is beyond the reach of the law [i.e. deceased] and that certain details have been disguised to hurt no one.

title: The Adventure of the Six Napoleons
label: The Adventure of the Six Napoleons
sentences: X1 of X2 brings X3 a mysterious problem about a man who shatters plaster busts of X4.
One was shattered in X5's shop, and two others, sold by X6 to a X7, were smashed after the doctor's house and branch office had been burgled.
Nothing else was taken.
In the former case, the bust was taken outside before being broken.
X3 knows that X8's theory about X9 lunatic must be wrong.
The busts in question all came from the same mould, when there are thousands of images of X4 all over X10.
The next day, X8 calls X3 to a house where there has been yet another bust-shattering, but there has also been a murder.
X11 found the dead man on his doorstep after investigating a noise.
His X4 bust was also taken by a burglar entering through a window.
It, too, was from the same mould.
Also, a photograph of a rather ape-ish-looking man is found in the dead man's pocket.
The fragments of X12's bust are in the front garden of an empty house up the street.
X3 concludes that the burglar wanted to see what he was doing, for there is a streetlamp here, whereas the bust could have been broken at another empty house nearer X12's, but it had been dark there.
X3 tells X8 to tell X12, a journalist for X13, that he is convinced that the culprit is a lunatic.
X3 knows that this is not true, but it is expedient to use the press to convince the culprit that this is what the investigators believe.
X3 interviews the two shopkeepers who sold the busts and finds out whom they were sold to, and where they were made, X14.
A couple of his informants also recognise the ape-ish man in the picture.
They know him as X15, an Italian immigrant.
He even worked in the shop where the first bust was broken, having left his job there only two days earlier.
X3 goes to X14 and finds out that the busts were part of a batch of six, but other than that, the manager can think of no reason why they should be special, or why anyone would want to destroy them.
He recognises X15's picture, and describes him as a rascal.
He was imprisoned for a street-fight stabbing a year earlier, but has likely been released now.
He once worked at X14, but has not been back.
His cousin still works there.
X3 begs the manager not to talk to the cousin about X15.
That evening, X8 brings news that the dead man has been identified as X16, a Mafioso.
X8 believes that X17 was sent to kill the culprit, but wound up dead himself.
After sending an express message, X3 invites X18 and X8 to join him outside a house in X19 where apparently X3 is expecting another bust-breaking.
X8 by now is exasperated with X3's preoccupation with the busts, but comes.
They are not disappointed.
X15 shows up, enters the house, and comes back out of the window minutes later with X20 bust, which he proceeds to shatter.
He then examines the pieces, quite unaware that X3 and X8 are sneaking up behind him.
They pounce, and X15 is arrested.
He will not talk, however.
The mystery is at last laid bare after X3 offers £10 (£ in ) to the owner of the last existing bust, making him sign a document transferring all rights and ownership of the bust to X3.
After the seller has left, X3 smashes the bust with a hunting crop.
Among the plaster shards is a gem, the black pearl of X21.
X3 was aware of the case of its disappearance from the beginning.
Suspicion had fallen on the owner's maid, whose X22 was X23's – the dead man's sister.
X15 somehow got the pearl from X16, and hid it inside a still-soft plaster bust at the factory where he worked, moments before his arrest for the street-fight stabbing.

title: The Adventure of the Three Students
label: The Adventure of the Three Students
sentences: X1 and X2 find themselves in a university town when a tutor and lecturer of X3, brings him an interesting problem.
X4 had been reviewing the galley proofs of an exam he was going to give when he left his office for an hour.

When he returned, he found that his servant, X5, had entered the room but accidentally left his key in the lock when he left, and someone had disturbed the exam papers on his desk and left traces that show it had been partially copied.
X5 is devastated and collapses on a chair, but swears that he did not touch the papers.
X4 found other clues in his office: pencil shavings, a broken pencil lead, a fresh cut in his desk surface, and a small blob of black clay speckled with sawdust.
X4 wants to uncover the cheater and prevent him from taking the exam, since it is for a sizeable scholarship.
Three students who will take the exam live above him in the same building.

The first, X6, is athletic, being a hurdler and a long-jumper, and industrious (in contrast to his father who squandered his fortune in horse racing); the second, X7, is described as quiet and methodical; the third is X8, a gifted man but thoroughly dissolute and given to gambling.
X9 examines the office.
The cheater obviously took the papers over to the window one by one while he copied them so that he could see X4 returning, but as it happens, X4 did not come back the usual way.
A nearby door leads to X4's bedroom.
Upon examining that, X9 finds another, similar, sawdust-speckled blob of clay.
He stuns X4 by telling him that the cheater, upon hearing his approach, hid in X4's bedroom.
He was there, hiding behind a curtain, all the time that X4 was questioning X5.
The next morning, X9 and X10 return to X4's office.
X9 confronts X5, accusing him of withholding information.
X5 will not own up to anything, and insists that there was no one in X4's office while he was there.
X9, however, sends for X6, and proceeds to lay out his results.
The cheater was someone who knew the exam proofs were there.
This could only be X6, because the proofs' whereabouts had been kept secret, and X6 was the only one tall enough to look in through X4's window to see his desk.
X9 has also identified the blobs as the special clay found in the long-jump pit, further implicating X6.
X6 reveals his guilt by reproaching X5 for his apparent treachery.
X5 was indeed the one who covered for X6.
He felt that he had to, for old times' sake: X5 was once X6's father's butler.
X9 then explains the remaining clues.
The scratch on the desk was caused by X6's spiked jumping shoes as he grabbed them in his haste, and the clay blobs fell from his shoes.
X5 had collapsed in the chair to hide X6's gloves, which he saw had been left on the chair.
For his part, X6 credits X5 with convincing him not to profit from his misdeed, and presents X4 with a letter stating his wish not to sit the exam, but to instead accept an offer to work for X11.

title: The Adventure of the Golden Pince-Nez
label: The Adventure of the Golden Pince-Nez
sentences: One wretched November night, X1 visits X2 at X3 to discuss the violent death of X4, secretary to X5 aged invalid X6.
X7 had dismissed his previous two secretaries.
The murder happened at X8 near X9, the fatal weapon being a sealing-wax knife belonging to the professor.
X10 can identify no motive for the killing, with X11 having no enemies or trouble in his past.
X11 was found by X7's maid, who recounts his last words as "The professor; it was she."
The maid further told X10 that before the murder, she heard X11 leave his room and walk down to the study; she had been hanging curtains and did not see him, only recognising his brisk step.
The professor was in bed at the time.
A minute later, a hoarse scream issued from the study, and the maid, hesitating briefly, entered and found the murder.
She later tells X2 that X11 went out for a walk not long before the murder.

The murderer's only likely means of entry was through the back door after walking along the path from the road, and X10 found some indistinct footmarks running beside the path, the murderer obviously seeking to leave no trail.
X10 could not tell whether the track was coming or going, nor whether made by big or small feet.
The professor's study contained a bureau; nothing seemed to have been stolen.
Its drawers were left open, as was normal, and the cupboard in the middle was locked.
The professor kept the key.
A lone piece of evidence was found in X4's hand: a pair of golden pince-nez spectacles.

X2 examines these and from them alone deduces the following details of the murderer: It is a woman; She is of some good breeding; She dresses like a lady; She is a person of refinement and is well dressed; She has a thick nose; Her eyes are close together; She has a puckered forehead, a peering look, and likely rounded shoulders; She has been to an optician at least twice over the last few months.
X12, and X10 head to X13 the next morning, and X2 carefully examines the site.
In the study, he notices a recent scratch on the bureau and reasons the murderer intended to access its contents.
X11 was killed as his presence interfered with the burglary.
No-one saw the murderer leave, nor did anyone hear a door opening.
X2 notes that both the corridors, the one leading from the back door and the one leading to the professor's bedroom, are about the same length and lined with coconut matting.
X2 interviews the professor in his bedroom, smoking many Egyptian cigarettes and dropping the ashes all over the floor.
The professor claims utter ignorance regarding the murder and ventures that X11's death may be suicide.
X2 asks about the locked cupboard in the bureau.
The professor hands over the key.
X2 inspects the key and returns it immediately, leaving the bureau sealed.
X14 asks X2 if he has a clue, and X2 tells him the cigarette ashes might reveal the truth.
X2 meets the housekeeper in the garden and has a seemingly unimportant conversation about the professor's eating habits; apparently, he has eaten heavily today.
In the afternoon, the three men return to the professor in his room, and X2 deliberately knocks the cigarettes over as an excuse to get a closer look at the floor.
X2's suspicion is confirmed – there are footprints in the ash.
At that moment, the murderer, appearing exactly as X2 deduced, emerges from a hiding place in a bookcase.
The mystery's explanation is revealed as: the woman came in secret to the professor's house to obtain some documents, using a duplicate key she gained from one of the former secretaries.
She was surprised by X11, whom she attacked with the nearest object to hand, the sealing-wax knife; she had not intended to kill him.
She lost her pince-nez in the scramble to escape; unable to see clearly, she turned along the wrong corridor and wound up in the professor's room.
Although surprised, he hid her.
The murderer is, in fact, the professor's estranged wife, X15, and they are both Russian.
Years prior, the pair had been involved with nihilists; she and a non-violent nihilist friend were both betrayed by the professor for gain.
Having finished her jail sentence in X16 came in search of evidence that would exonerate her friend.
X15 had met X11 while he was taking his walk, explaining X11's last words.
The professor's increased appetite is, of course, explained by his having to feed a second, hidden person.

title: The Adventure of the Missing Three-Quarter
label: The Adventure of the Missing Three-Quarter
sentences: X1 of X2, comes to X3 seeking his help in X4's disappearance.

X5 is the star player on X6's rugby union team (who plays at the three-quarters position, hence the story's title) and they will likely lose an important match the following day against X7 if X5 cannot be found.
X8 has to admit that amateur sport is outside his field of expertise, but he shows the same care he has shown to his other cases.
X5 had seemed a bit pale and bothered earlier in the day.

Later in the evening, according to a hotel porter, a rough-looking, bearded man came to the hotel with a note for X5; judging from the young man's reaction, the note contained rather devastating news.
He immediately left the hotel with the bearded stranger; the two of them were last seen running in the direction of X9 at about half past ten.
No one has seen them since.
X6 has wired to X10, but X5 has not been seen there.
He has also wired X11's very wealthy uncle and nearest living relative, but has heard no answer.
X5 is the almost-eighty-year-old X12's heir, but he must meanwhile live in relative poverty owing to his uncle's miserly behaviour.
X8 further questions the porter.
The bearded man who brought the note was neither a gentleman nor a workman, and he seemed to be bothered by something too, for his hand was trembling as he handed the porter the note to give to X5.
The only word that the porter overheard of their short conversation was "time".
Earlier in the evening, at six o'clock, the porter had brought X5 a telegram, and saw X5 write a reply.
X5 told the porter that he would send it himself.
X8 looks at the telegraph forms in X5's room, and then at the blotter, finally finding a clue.
The impression on the blotter yields a part of the message that X5 sent: "Stand by us for God's sake".
Obviously at least one other person is involved ("us"), and there is some kind of danger.
X12 briefly visits, but can give X8 no useful information as to his nephew's whereabouts.
The old miser seems utterly aghast at the possibility that it might be a kidnapping whose object would be to extort his wealth.
X8 and X13 then go to the telegraph office, where X8 uses a ruse to get the woman there to show him the counterfoil of the message that X5 sent.
It was addressed to X14, a medical academic at X10.
X8 and X13 go to see X15, who tells them that X5 is an intimate friend of his.
He does not react when told that X5 has disappeared, and claims not to know where he is, and not to have seen him recently.
However, when X8 produces a bill for services issued by X15 to X16 furiously refuses to answer any more questions, denies that he had the telegram from X5, and has his butler show X8 and X13 out.
X8 deduces that X15 must know where X5 is, and lodges at an inn just across the street from X15's office to keep watch.
X8 learns that X15, although not in actual medical practice, regularly rides in his brougham out into the country somewhere.
The round trip seems to take about three hours.
X8 tries following the brougham on one of its outings, but is thwarted by X17, who makes it quite clear that he is aware that X8 is following him.
The next day, X8's inquiries in all the local villages come to naught; no one has seen the doctor's brougham passing through.
The mystery is at last unlocked by X18, a beagle-foxhound cross.
After X8 covertly sprays aniseed oil onto the wheels of the doctor's brougham, X18 tracks it to a cottage in the countryside.
What X8 finds there is not pleasant.
X5 is there, but is grieving over his young wife, who has just died of consumption.
Her existence was kept secret, because X12 would not have approved of the marriage and would have disowned his nephew.
X15 had told the woman's father about her condition, and he, the bearded stranger, had unwisely told X5, who felt compelled to rush off forthwith.
X8 tells X15 that as long as there is no foul play involved, private affairs are not his business.
He and X13 then depart, leaving X5 to his grief.

title: The Adventure of the Abbey Grange
label: The Adventure of the Abbey Grange
sentences: X1 wakes up X2 early one winter morning to rush to a murder scene at the X3 near X4.
X5 has been killed, apparently by burglars.
X6 believes that it was the infamous X7 gang who have committed several other burglaries in the neighbourhood.
At X8 tells X9 that her marriage was not happy; X10 was a violent, abusive drunkard.
She then tells that about 11 o'clock, in the dining room, she encountered an elderly man coming in the French window, followed by two younger men.
The older man struck her in the face, knocking her out.
When she came to, she was gagged and tied to an oaken chair with the bellrope, which they had torn down.
X10 came into the room and rushed at the intruders, one of whom struck and killed him with a poker.
X11 fainted again for a minute or two.
She saw the intruders drinking wine from a bottle taken from the sideboard.
Then they left, taking some silver plate.
X10's corpse is still lying at the murder scene.
X12 tells X9 some unsavoury things about X10: that he poured petroleum over his wife's dog and set it alight, and once threw a decanter at her X13.
X14 corroborates X11's account of X10 being an abusive alcoholic.
Examining the bellrope, X9 notes that if it was tugged hard enough to tear it down, the bell would have rung in the kitchen, and asks why nobody heard it.
X12 answers that it was late, and the kitchen is at the back of the house, where none of the servants would have heard.
This suggests that the burglars must have known this, indicating a link between them and one of the servants.
Oddly, the thieves stole only a few items of silver plate from the dining room.

The half-empty wine bottle and glasses interest X9 – the cork had been drawn with the corkscrew of a "multiplex knife", not the long corkscrew in the drawer, and one of the glasses has beeswing dregs in it, but the others have none.
Annoyed at being called to investigate a case that apparently has a ready-made solution, X9 decides to catch the train back to X15.
However, after having mulled things over during the journey, X9 thinks that X11's story has too many holes in it and that probably she and X14 have lied deliberately, staging a false crime scene.
Upon returning to the X16, after examining again the supposed crime scene, reaches this conclusion: the killer cut the bellrope with a knife, and frayed the loose end to make it look broken.
X9 confronts X11 and X14, telling them he knows they are lying and demanding the truth, but they stand by their story.
On the way out, X9 notices a hole in the ice on the pond, and writes a note for X12.
X9 searches for the killer: almost certainly a sailor (indicated by the knots and the active physique) who was previously acquainted with X11, and whom she and X14 would protect.
X11 travelled by the ocean liner of X17, which is now halfway to X18.
However, the ship's first officer, X19, who has been promoted to captain, has remained in X20 and in two days will take command of the company's new ship, X21.
X9 takes a cab to X22 but does not go in.
He tells X23 he is reluctant to name the criminal to the police until he knows more.
That evening, X12 calls at X24, with two items of news: As suggested in X9's note, the stolen silver was found at the bottom of the pond.
X9 suggests that the theft was a blind—a deliberate false clue.
However, X12 rationalises that the pond was chosen as a temporary hiding place.
The X7 gang was arrested in X25 that morning, so they couldn't have committed a murder in X26 the previous night.
Later that evening, X27 comes to X28, summoned by a telegram from X9.
X9 demands a full account of what happened at the X3, warning X29 that X9 will summon the police if he lies or conceals anything.
X29 met a X30), on the voyage from X18.
He fell in love with her, but not she with him.
Then he happened to meet X14, who told him of X10's abusive behaviour.
He met secretly with X31 at the house; the last time on the previous night.
They were in the dining room when X10 burst in, insulted X31, and struck her with a cudgel.

title: The Adventure of the Second Stain
label: The Adventure of the Second Stain
sentences: X1, the Prime Minister, and X2, the Secretary of State for European Affairs, come to X3 in the matter of a document stolen from X4's dispatch box, which he kept at home in X5 when not at work.
If divulged, this document could bring about very dire consequences for all of X6, even war.
They are loath to tell X3 at first the exact nature of the document's contents, but when X3 declines to take on their case, they tell him it was a rather injudicious letter from a foreign potentate.
It disappeared from the dispatch box one evening when X4's wife was out at the theatre for four hours.
No one in the house knew about the document, not even the Secretary's wife.
None of the servants could have guessed what was in the box.
X3 decides to begin with some spies known to him and is then astonished to hear from X7 that one of those that he names, X8, has been murdered.
Before X3 has a chance to act, X9, the European Secretary's wife, arrives unexpectedly at X10.
She asks X3 insistently about the stolen document's contents, but X3 only reveals there would be regrettable consequences if the document were not found.
X11 also begs X3 to tell her husband nothing of her visit.
X3's spy hunt does not go well.
Four days after the murder, French police arrest the probable murderer of X12, whom X13 married in X14 under an alias.
She was seen in X15 near X13's house the night of the crime, but she is now useless as a witness because she has gone insane.
X16 calls X3 to the murder scene to examine something odd.
X13 bled over a drugget, and the blood soaked through it, but curiously there is no bloodstain on the floor under the drugget.
However, there is one under the opposite edge of the carpet.
It can only mean that the constable guarding the crime scene has been foolish enough to let someone in and leave them alone while they moved things in the room, including the carpet.
X3 tells X17 to take the constable to a back room and obtain a confession, which he does vigorously.
Meanwhile, X3 pulls the unfastened carpet aside and quickly finds a hiding place in the floor, but it is empty.
The errant constable tells X3 that the unauthorised visitor was a young woman.
She apparently fainted at the sight of the blood but had left while the constable went out to fetch some brandy to revive her.
As X3 is leaving X13's house, he shows the constable a photograph, and he recognises it as the visitor.
X3 goes to the X4's household and confronts X11, accusing her of the theft.
At first, she denies everything, but is forced to admit her wrongdoing under the threat of certain scandal.
X11 admits X13 was blackmailing her with a compromising letter written by her years earlier, and demanded the document as payment (an unnamed spy had made X13 aware of the document).
X11 went to X13's house to do the business when, as it happened, his wife from X14 showed up and confronted him about his affair, believing X11 was his mistress.
X11 hurriedly left, albeit not before seeing X13 place the document under the drugget.
She returned to fetch the document after her visit to X3 convinced her she needed to do so.
She hands the document to X3.
At X3's suggestion, the document is put back in the dispatch box using X11's duplicate key.
When X4 arrives back home with the Prime Minister, X3 pretends to believe that the evidence has convinced him that the document must still be in the box, shuffled between other papers.
It is soon found, and X4 rejoices that it was apparently only a mistake.
The Prime Minister suspects X3 knows more than he is telling, but X3 simply responds, "We also have our diplomatic secrets."

title: The Adventure of Wisteria Lodge
label: The Adventure of Wisteria Lodge
sentences: X1 is visited by X2, who wishes to discuss something "grotesque".
No sooner has he arrived at X3 than X4 also shows up, along with X5 of the X6.
They wish a statement from X7 about the murder of X8 near X9 the previous night.
X7 explains that he spent the night at X10's rented house, but when he woke up in the morning, he found that X11 and his servants had all disappeared, leaving him alone in the house.
X7 mentions that a note, delivered during dinner the previous evening, had caused great consternation to X11 and may have had some connection with the household's disappearance.

The story told by him seems inconsistent with the physical evidence, yet the policemen never doubt his story, demonstrating to X12 that X7 must have been invited to provide a fake alibi, which would have carried much weight by virtue of him being an extremely proper and respectable gentleman.
X12's investigation leads him to X13 household, whose master has spent time in the tropics, and whose secretary is a dark-skinned foreigner.
X12 believes that the cryptic note came from this household and the writer could only be the house's governess, X14, who has not been seen since the night of the murder.
That night, the X15 flee by train.
X14 escapes with the help of a former gardener.
It is revealed that "X16" is in fact X17, an overthrown dictator from X18 who left a bloody trail behind as he escaped to X19.
X14's real name is X20.
Her late husband was X21's ambassador to X22 and a potential political rival to X23.
X23 had him recalled and shot so that he would not pose a threat to X23's position.
Fortunately, X24 stayed behind in X19 and avoided harm herself.
She went on to change her name and secure the position as governess to X16's children in order to get closer to and spy on him.
X23 and his secretary give the police the slip in X25, and resurface in X26 under new aliases.
However, they are both murdered, and their killers are never caught.

title: The Adventure of the Red Circle
label: The Adventure of the Red Circle
sentences: X1, a landlady, comes to X2 with some questions about her new lodger, who is renting a room on the top floor of her house.

A youngish, heavily bearded man, who spoke good but accented English, came to her and offered double her usual rent on the condition that he receive a key to the house and was not to be disturbed for any reason.
He went out the first night that he was there, and came back after midnight when the rest of the household had gone to bed.
Since then, neither X1, her husband, nor their servant girl has seen him.
He requests items via printed notes, and his meals are to be left on a chair outside the door.
After the landlady leaves, X3 remarks to X4 that it seems likely that the person in X1's house is not the bearded man who made the arrangements.
X3 determines that messages are being sent to the lodger in the form of advertisements placed in a particular newspaper, which X1 leaves by the door each morning.
X3 and X5 go to X1's house and spy on the lodger, who they discover to be a young woman with a dark complexion.
That evening, X3 and X5 are on hand to see her confederate send messages by a waving candle.
X3 and X5 meet X6 and a X7 detective from X8.
They are lying in wait for X9, a vicious killer.
Upon entering the room from which the signal originated, they discover X10 lying on the floor in a pool of blood, dead from a stab wound to the throat.
The lodger is revealed as X11, and her confederate is X12, her husband.
She confirms that the couple were seeking refuge from X10, who was out to kill X12 for betraying the X13, a secret Italian criminal organization to which they had both belonged.
X12 decided to leave the organization in spite of the threatened consequences.
He and his wife fled X14 and went to X15 to escape the X13, but X10 tracked X12 down and attacked while he was trying to signal X16.
X17 takes X16 down to the police station, but comments that she and X12 will likely face no criminal charges over X10's death.

title: The Adventure of the Bruce-Partington Plans
label: The Adventure of the Bruce-Partington Plans
sentences: The monotony of X1 thick smog-shrouded X2 is broken by a sudden visit from X3.
He has come about some missing, secret submarine plans.
Seven of the ten plans have been found with X4's body, but the three "most essential" papers are still missing.
X5 was a young clerk in a government office at X6, whose body was found next to the X7 tracks near X8 tube station, his head crushed.
He had little money with him (although there appears to have been no robbery), theatre tickets, and curiously, no X7 ticket.
X9 tells X10 that a passenger reported hearing a thud, as though a body had fallen on the track, close to where X5's body was found.
The passenger could not see anything, however, owing to the thick fog.

After an examination of the track near X11 concludes that X5 had been killed elsewhere, was deposited on the roof of an X7 train, and fell off when the jarring action of going across a railway point at X12 shook the coach.
X10 decides to visit X13, who was in charge of the papers.
He has, however, died, apparently of a broken heart from the loss of his honour when the papers were stolen, according to his brother X14.

On visiting X5's fiancée, X10 learns that X5 had something on his mind for the last week or so of his life; he had commented on how easily a traitor could get hold of "the secret" and how much foreign agents would pay for it.
On the night in question, X5 and his fiancée were on their way to the theatre, when he suddenly dashed off into the fog and did not return.
X10 next goes to the office from which the plans were stolen.
X15, the senior clerk, tells X10 that, as always, he was the last man out of the office that night, and that he had put the papers in the safe.

Anyone coming in afterwards to steal them would have needed three keys (for the building, the office, and the safe), but no duplicates were found on X5's body, and only the late X16 had all three keys.
X17 also mentions that one of the seven recovered papers includes a unique invention, without which the submarine could not be properly built.
X10 also discovers that it is possible to see what is happening inside the office from outside, as the iron shutters do not close properly.
After leaving, X10 finds that the clerk at the nearby X7 station remembers seeing X5 on the evening in question.
Deeply shaken by something, he had taken a train to X18.
Acting on information from X19, and on what he has learnt thus far, X10 identifies a person of interest: X20, a known foreign agent who left town shortly after X5's murder.
Some small reconnaissance shows X10 that X21's house backs onto an above-ground portion of the X7 line; furthermore, owing to traffic at a nearby junction, trains often stop right under his windows.
It seems clear that X5's body was laid on the train roof just there.
X10 and X22 break into X21's empty house and closely examine the windows, finding that the grime has been smudged, and there is a bloodstain.
An underground train stops right under the window.
Some messages from X23's agony column, all seeming to allude to a business deal, are also found, posted by "X24".
X10 posts a similarly cryptic message in the X25 demanding a meeting, signing it X24, in the hopes that the thief might show up at X21's house.
X14 shows up and is stunned to find X26, and X19 all waiting for him.
He confesses to the theft of the plans, but swears that it was X21 who killed X5.
X5 had followed the X27 to X21's and then intervened, and X21 had dealt X5 a fatal blow to the head.
X21 then decided, over the X27's objections, that he had to keep three of the papers, because they could not be copied in a short time.
He then got the idea of putting the other seven in X5's pocket and putting him on a train roof outside his window, reasoning that he would be blamed for the theft when his body was found.
Deep in debt, X28 had acted out of a need for money.
He redeems himself somewhat by agreeing to write to X21, whose address X29 he knows, inviting him to come back to X30 for the fourth, vital page.
This ruse also works; X21 is imprisoned, and the missing pages of the plans are recovered from his trunk.
X28 dies in prison, not long after starting his sentence.
For his efforts, X10 is given an emerald tie pin by "a certain gracious lady", implied to be X31, as the pin was received at X32 in the 1890s.

title: The Adventure of the Dying Detective
label: The Adventure of the Dying Detective
sentences: X1 is called to tend X2, who is apparently dying of a rare tropical disease, X3 fever, contracted while he was on a case.
X4 is shocked, not having heard about his friend's illness.
X5 says that X2 has neither eaten nor drunk anything in three days.
X2 instructs X4 not to come near him, because the illness is highly infectious.
In fact, he scorns to be treated by X4 and insults his abilities, astonishing and hurting the doctor.
Although X4 wishes to examine X2 himself or call in a specialist, X2 demands that X4 wait several hours before seeking help.
While X4 waits, he examines several objects in X2's room.
X2 grows angry when X4 touches a small ivory box, ordering X4 to put it down and sit still.
At six o'clock, X2 tells X4 to turn the gaslight on, but only half-full.
He then instructs X4 to bring X6 of X7 to see X2, but to make sure that X4 returns to X8 before X9 arrives.
X4 goes to X9's address.
Although X9 refuses to see anyone, X4 forces his way in.
Once X4 explains his errand on behalf of X10's attitude changes drastically.
X9 agrees to come to X8 within a half hour.
X4 excuses himself, saying that he has another appointment; he returns before X9's arrival and, at X2's instruction, conceals himself behind the head of X2's bed.
Believing that they are alone, X9 is frank with X2.
It emerges, to the hiding X4's horror, that X2 has been sickened by the same illness that killed X11.
X9 then sees the little ivory box, which he had sent to X2 by post, and which contains a sharp spring infected with the illness.
X9 pockets it, removing the evidence of his crime.
He then resolves to stay there and watch X2 die.
X2 asks X9 to turn the gas up full, which X9 does.
X9 then asks X2 if he would like anything else, to which X2 replies - no longer in the voice of a man near death - "a match and a cigarette."
X12 then enters, as the full gaslight was the signal to move in.
X2 tells X13 to arrest X9 for the murder of his nephew, and perhaps also for the attempted murder of X2 himself.
X9 points out that his word is as good as X2's in court, but X2 then calls for X4 to emerge from hiding, to present himself as another witness to the conversation.
X2 explains that he feigned his illness as a ruse to induce X9 to confess to his nephew's murder.
X2 was not infected by the little box, having learned to take precautions about his incoming mail due to the number of enemies he has made.

Starving himself for three days and the claim of the "disease's" infectious nature was to keep X4 from examining him and discovering the ruse, since, as he clarifies, he has every respect for his friend's medical skills.

title: The Disappearance of Lady Frances Carfax
label: The Disappearance of Lady Frances Carfax
sentences: X1 sends X2 to X3 to investigate X4's disappearance since he himself is too busy in X5.
X6 is a lone, unwed woman denied a rich inheritance on account of her sex.
She does, however, carry valuable jewels with her.
It is also her habit to write to her old governess, X7, every other week, but for the past five weeks, there has not been a word from her.
She has left the X8 in X3 for parts unknown.
Her last two bank transactions were cheques, one to pay her hotel bill, and another for £50 to her maid, X9.
In X10 finds out that X6 stayed at the X8 for several weeks, but then suddenly left in a hurry one day.
Only one witness could suggest an explanation, one involving a big, bearded man who kept hounding her.
It also emerges that X6's maid has left her employ, although it is not known why.
X11 finds out where X6 went, and inquires at X12 in X13.
She stayed there for a fortnight and met a couple described as X14, a convalescent missionary and biblical scholar from X15, and his wife.
X6 left with them three weeks ago for X5, and nothing has been heard of her since.
X11 also finds out that the big bearded man, the "savage", came about a week ago looking for her.
X11 telegraphs X16 about his progress, and oddly, X16 wires back asking for a description of X14's left ear.
X11 believes this to be X16's attempt at humour.
X16 is actually in earnest.
X11 visits X17, the former maid, in X18, and it turns out that her upcoming wedding was why she left X6's employ.
The £50 was a wedding present.
She, too, believes that the bearded man was the reason that her former mistress left X3.
He was quite a rough man.
During this interview, X19 sees the very man in question in the street.
X11 rushes out and demands to know who he is and what he has done with X6.
A fight ensues and X11 is nearly strangled.
A French workman breaks the fight up with his cudgel and the bearded man withdraws.

It then turns out that the workman is X20 disguised X16, who suggests that X11 accompany him back to X5, and wryly observes that there is no blunder which X11 has failed to commit in this investigation.
Before leaving, however, X16 interviews someone.
It is the bearded man, X21, an old suitor of X6's.
Yes, he is seeking X6, but he still wants to win her heart.
As a younger man, despite being the son of a famous Admiral, he was not rich.
Now that he has made his fortune in X22, he hopes she will see him differently, but he is still rather churlish and clearly X6 is unwilling.
X16 recommends that he go back to X5.
Once X16 and X11 are back at X23 reads a telegram from X24 about X14's left ear—"jagged or torn".
This confirms X16's suspicion that X14 is in fact X25, a vicious rascal from X26 (his earlobe was chewed away in a bar brawl).
His so-called wife's real name is X27.
He beguiles young women by playing to their religious beliefs, as X28 did with X6.
This suggested his true identity to X16.
X16 believes that X6 is in X5, and quite possibly dead, or if not, confined in some way.
The search seems hopeless.
The police follow known associates, X16 places advertisements hoping to learn something, but nothing happens.
Then, a pawnshop reports that someone matching X28's description has pawned a pendant very much like one owned by X6.

title: The Adventure of the Devil's Foot
label: The Adventure of the Devil's Foot
sentences: X1 and X2 find themselves at X3 in X4 one spring.
The holiday is interrupted when the local vicar and his lodger visit X5, asking for his assistance.
The night before, X6 had gone to visit his three siblings, played whist with them, and then left.
The next morning, the housekeeper found the trio still sitting in their places at the table; the X7 had gone insane, and the X8 was dead.
X9, a famous hunter-explorer and a cousin of the X10, aborts his sailing from X11 after the vicar wires him with the tragic news.
He asks X5 what his suspicions are, and is displeased when X5 will not voice any.
The next morning, the vicar informs X5 that X12 has died in the same way as his sister.
The two men, along with X13, rush to X14's room.
A lamp is lit and smoking on the table beside the dead man.

X5 deduces that a poison, activated by combustion and affecting the cognitive functions, is the murder weapon; a fire was burning in the first murder room and a lamp in the second, and people who entered them either felt ill or fainted.

After a dangerous experiment in which he tests the residue of the poison on himself and is only just rescued by X15 reveals that X12 is guilty of the first crime and further deduces that X16 was X14's murderer.
X16 confesses that he held X14 at gunpoint and forced him to breathe the poison.
It comes from a plant X17.
X18 once described the powder to X12, who stole some from X18's collection of African curiosities, then attempted to murder his siblings by throwing it on the fire just before he left.
It is revealed that X18 was passionately in love with X19, but was still married to and unable to divorce his first wife who had abandoned him years ago.
X5's sympathies in this matter lie with X18, and he tells him to go back to his work in X20 and never return.

title: His Last Bow (short story)
label: His Last Bow (short story)
sentences: On the eve of X1, the German agent is getting ready to leave X2 with his vast collection of intelligence, gathered over a four-year period.
His wife and household have already left X3 for X4 in X5, leaving only him and his elderly English housekeeper.
X6's associate, X7, a German diplomat from X8, is impressed by his acquisition of vital British military secrets, and tells X6 that he will be received in X9 as a hero.
X6 says that he is waiting for one last transaction with his Irish-American informant, who will arrive shortly with a rich treasure: naval signals.
X10 leaves just before X11 arrives.
X6's housekeeper has turned her light off and retired.
X11 shows X6 a package.
X11 disparages X6's safe, but X6 proudly says that its construction and the double combination lock make it impenetrable.
He tells X11 that the combination is "August 1914".
X11, mentioning cases in which several German informants have ended up in prison, is distrustful of X6 and refuses to deliver the naval codes until he receives payment.
X6 refuses to pay until he has examined X11's intelligence data.
X11 hands him the package.
X6 finds that it is a book titled X12, hardly what he expected.
Even less expected is the chloroform-soaked rag that is held in his face by X11 a moment later.
X11 is actually X13 in disguise, and the chauffeur who brought him is X14.

Now past their heyday, they have nonetheless caught several spies (X15 is actually responsible for the imprisoned agents of whom "X11" spoke), and fed the Germans some thoroughly untrustworthy intelligence.
X15 had retired from detective work, spending his days beekeeping in the countryside, but returned after the Foreign Minister and the Premier came to him.

X15 has been on this case for two years, and it has taken him to X16, and X17, where he learnt to play the part of a bitter Irish-American, even gaining the credentials of a member of a secret society.
He identified the security leak through which British secrets were reaching the Germans, and then set out to apprehend the receiving agents themselves.
The housekeeper was one of X15's agents: the light that she switched off was the signal to X15 and X18 that the coast was clear.
X15 and X18 take X6 and the evidence to X19.
In reference to the impending War, X15 says, "There's an east wind coming, X18."
X18 misinterprets the meaning of the words and says, "I think not, X15.
It is very warm", to which X15 replies: "Good old X18!
You are the one fixed point in a changing age.
There's an east wind coming all the same, such a wind as never blew on X2 yet.
It will be cold and bitter, X18, and a good many of us may wither before its blast.
But it's X20's own wind none the less, and a cleaner, better, stronger land will lie in the sunshine when the storm has cleared."

title: The Adventure of the Mazarin Stone
label: The Adventure of the Mazarin Stone
sentences: X1 arrives in X2 where the page boy shows him a wax effigy of X3 placed near a curtained window in the sitting room.
The effigy produces a shadow on the curtain that, when viewed from outside, is the unmistakable profile of X4.
Using this visual trick, X3 aims to give a perfect target to a would-be murderer with a rifle.
X3 names his murderer as X5, the diamond thief he has been following in disguise.
He gives the criminal's address to X1, then sends the doctor out the back for the police.
As the Count arrives, X3 has X6 invite him inside, then takes him by surprise when he attempts an assault on the effigy.
X3 then offers the Count and his helper, X7, freedom if they give up the jewel, or jail if not.
He invites them to discuss the deal while he plays violin in the next room.

When the Count decides to double-cross X3 and takes the stone from his secret pocket to show X8 in window light, the detective springs from the chair in place of his replica and grabs the £100,000 jewel.
His bedroom has a gramophone and secret passage to behind the curtain.
After the police take away the villains, X9 – described by X3 as "the eminent peer who represents the very highest interests" – sweeps in.
Unlike the Prime Minister and Home Secretary, he did not want X3.
When tricked into insisting on arrest for whoever is found possessing the diamond, he finds the jewel in his pocket – where X3 has placed it – and apologizes.
Finally, X3 can eat.

title: The Problem of Thor Bridge
label: The Problem of Thor Bridge
sentences: X1 and former senator from "some Western state", approaches X2 to investigate the murder of his wife in order to clear his children's X3 of the crime.
It soon emerges that X4's marriage had been unhappy and he treated his wife very badly.
He had fallen in love with her when he met her in X5, but soon realised they had nothing in common.
He became attracted to X6; since he could not marry her, he had attempted to please her in other ways, such as trying to help people less fortunate than himself.
X7 was found lying in a pool of blood on X8 with a bullet through the head and note from the governess, agreeing to a meeting at that location, in her hand.
A recently discharged revolver with one shot fired is found in X6's wardrobe.
X9 agrees to look at the situation in spite of the damning evidence.
From the outset, X9 observes some rather odd things about the case.
How could X6 so coolly and rationally have planned and carried out the murder and then carelessly tossed the murder weapon into her wardrobe?
What was the strange chip on the underside of the bridge's stone balustrade?
Why was X10 clutching the note from X6 when she died?
If the murder weapon was one of a matched pair of pistols, why couldn't the other one be found in X4's collection?

X9 uses his powers of deduction to solve the crime, and demonstrates, using X11's revolver, how it was perpetrated: X10, outraged and jealous of X6's relationship with her husband, resolved to end her own life and frame her rival for the crime.

After arranging a meeting with X6, requesting her to leave her response in a note, X10 tied a rock on a piece of string to the end of a revolver, and shot herself, the rock pulling the revolver over the side of the bridge; the revolver found in X6's wardrobe was the other pistol of the pair, which had been fired off in the woods earlier, and the chip in the bridge was caused by the pistol hitting the stonework as it was pulled off by the rock.
X9's reconstruction reproduces the damage to the balustrade of the bridge.
He asks the police to drag the lake for the revolvers of X11 and X12.

title: The Adventure of the Creeping Man
label: The Adventure of the Creeping Man
sentences: A X1, the personal secretary of X2, comes to X3 with a most unusual problem.
He is engaged to the professor's daughter, and the Professor is himself engaged to a young lady, although he himself is already 61 years of age.
Their impending marriage has caused no scandal, but the trouble seems to have begun at about the time of the engagement.
First, the professor suddenly left home for a fortnight without telling anyone of his destination, with the family later learning that he had been to X4.
Upon returning, X5 unprecedentedly forbade X6 from opening certain stamped letters.
The professor had also brought a carved wooden box from X4, and became very angry with X6 for touching it.

The whole household also observes severe changes in the man's personality: he has become furtive and sly, with changes in his moods and habits, some of which are quite bizarre, though not impeding his functions.

X6 notes particularly strange incidents: one, in which he saw the professor crawling along the hall on his hands and feet and his master swore him off; and another, witnessed by X7, who saw her father at two o'clock in the morning at her bedroom window on the second floor.
Further, the professor's usually faithful Irish Wolfhound has started attacking him (X3 notes this happens at 9 day intervals), and has to be chained up outside.
X3 and X8 go to the university city to see the professor.
They pretend that they have an appointment, but the professor sees through the ruse and becomes furiously angry at the intrusion.
X6 dissuades the professor from violence.
X3 and X8 leave with X3 confiding to X8 that the visit has taught him that the professor's mind is clear and functional despite recent behaviour.
X6 tells X3 that he has found the address of the mysterious letters.
The addressee is a man X9, a Central European name, fitting with the professor's secret journey to X4.
X3 later finds out from X10, his "general utility man", that X11 is indeed an elderly Bohemian who keeps a large general store.
X3 examines X12's bedroom window, finding that the only way to climb up to it is using the creeper, unusual for a 61-year-old man.
X3 forms a theory that every 9 days X2 takes some drug which causes the odd behaviour, having become addicted in X4, and is supplied by X11 in X13.
X3 also comes to realise, by connecting the professor's thick and horny knuckles, his odd behaviour, the dog's attacks, and the use of the creeper, that the professor is behaving like a monkey.
Shortly after the realisation, X3 and X8 are treated to a firsthand display of X2's odd behaviour.
He comes out of the house, scampers about on all fours, climbs on the creeper, and torments the tied-up dog.
Unfortunately, the wolfhound gets loose and attacks the professor.
The two of them, with X14's help, get the dog off the professor who is wounded badly.
X8 and X6, also a medical man, tend to the professor's injuries.
X3 then examines the professor's little wooden box after having obtained the key from the unconscious owner.
It contained a drug, as X3 expected, but also a letter from a X15, whom X8 reveals to be a notorious quack.
The professor had sought out X16's rejuvenation treatments due to his upcoming marriage to a younger woman.
The drug's effects are explained as a consequence of being obtained from langurs.
Promising to hold X16 responsible, X3 muses on the consequences of such drugs and departs with X8.

title: The Adventure of the Sussex Vampire
label: The Adventure of the Sussex Vampire
sentences: X1 receives an odd letter that makes reference to vampires.
X2, who comes to X3 the next morning, has become convinced that his Peruvian second wife has been sucking their baby son's blood.
By his first wife, he has a 15-year-old X4, who suffered an unfortunate accident as a child and now, although he can still walk, does not have full use of his legs.
Since the start of the bloodsucking, X5 has unaccountably been struck twice by his stepmother, although X6 cannot imagine why.
Ever since being found out by her husband, she has locked herself in her room and refused to come out.
Only her Peruvian X7 is allowed in.
She takes X8 her meals.
Even before X1 and X9 set off for X6's house in X10 has worked out what is going on, and it has nothing to do with vampires.
X1's trip is made simply to observe and confirm what he has already deduced.
Upon their arrival in X11's maid announces that her mistress is ill, and X12 offers to help.
He finds an agitated woman in the room upstairs – she speaks of all being destroyed, and of sacrificing herself rather than breaking her husband's heart.
She also demands her child, who has been with the nurse ever since X6 found out about the bloodsucking incidents.
X1 examines the South American weapons displayed in the house and meets the children.
While X6 is doting on his younger son, X9 notices that X1 is gazing at the window.
He cannot imagine why his friend is doing this.
X1 then reveals the truth about what has been happening, much to the relief of X8 as this is exactly what she has been hoping for: the truth to come from someone else's lips.
It turns out that the culprit is X13's elder son, who is extremely jealous of his young half-brother.
X1 has confirmed this by looking at X5's reflection in the window while his father's attention was on the baby.
X5 has been attempting to murder his half-brother by shooting poisoned darts at him, and his stepmother's behaviour of sucking the baby's neck is thereby explained: she was sucking the poison out.
It also explains why she struck X5, and why she was sick when X1 and X9 arrived.
The wounds, therefore, were caused by the darts, not by her biting.
X8 had not wanted to be the one to tell her husband what X5 had done.

title: The Adventure of the Three Garridebs
label: The Adventure of the Three Garridebs
sentences: X1 receives a letter from a X2, in which the writer asks for help in finding someone else who shares his unusual surname.
He has been informed by an American, X3, that if he can find another X4 he stands to inherit a large fortune.
The American visits X1 and X5 at X6, and is not pleased that X7 has involved a private detective.

X8, who claims to be a lawyer, tells a story about meeting a millionaire land tycoon in X9, who bequeathed his $15 million estate to X10, with the proviso that he find two more men of the same surname to share it with equally.
X10 says he has come to X11 to seek out people with this name, having failed to find anyone in his home country.
So far, he has found only X7.
X1 deduces that X8 has been in X12 for some time, and is not newly arrived as he claims.
When X1 invents a fictitious X13 politician, X8 says he once knew him.
X1 does not reveal that he knows X8 is lying, and instead arranges to meet X14.
Upon arrival at X15 observes X14's nameplate outside the house.
It has obviously been there for years, leading X1 to conclude that this is his real name.
X14 is an elderly eccentric who collects everything from ancient coins to old bones.
X7's rooms look like a museum, but he holds nothing of financial value.
It is not clear what the American might be after.
During the visit, X8 arrives, having supposedly found a newspaper advertisement purportedly placed by X16 in the course of his everyday business.
X1 observes that X8 must have placed the advertisement himself as the terms and spelling are distinctly American.
Despite X7's objections, X8 insists that he must travel to X17 and meet this X18.
X1 realizes that the whole scheme is X8's way to get X7 out of the way for a while.
Next day, X1 goes to see X19 at X20 and identifies X8 as X21, who has escaped from prison after shooting three men in X22.
In X12, he had killed X23, a forger X24 whose description matches the former occupant of X14's room.
X1 and X5 go to X4's home armed with revolvers.
They do not have to wait long before X25 arrives.
From their hiding place, X1 and X5 see the criminal use a "jemmy" to open a trapdoor, revealing a little cellar.
They capture X25, but not before he manages to shoot twice, striking X5 in the leg.
X1 is distraught over X5's injury, and strikes X25 on the head with the butt of a gun hard enough to draw blood.
Fortunately, X5's wound is superficial.
The cellar contains a printing press and stacks of counterfeit banknotes, hidden there by X26, the man that X25 had killed.
X25 is sent back to prison.
X14 ends up in a nursing home, so great is his disappointment, but many X27 are pleased that X26's equipment has at last been found.

Despite being hurt, X5 seems the happiest at the adventure's outcome, declaring, from the sight of X1's panic and rage over his friend's shooting, that "It was worth a wound, it was worth many wounds, to know the depth of loyalty and love which lay behind that cold mask".

title: The Adventure of the Illustrious Client
label: The Adventure of the Illustrious Client
sentences: X1 comes to see X2 and X3 about a problem faced by a client of his, whom he refuses to name and whose connection to the matter at hand must not become public knowledge.
X4, a friend of the client, has a young daughter who has fallen in love with X5 roguish and sadistic Austrian X6.
X7 and X2 are convinced that X8 is a shameless philanderer and a murderer.
His victim was his last wife, of whose murder he was acquitted owing to a legal technicality and a witness's untimely death.
She met her end in X9.
X2 also finds out that the Baron has expensive tastes and is a collector and a recognised authority on Chinese pottery.
X2's first step is to see X8, who is amused to see X2 trying to "play a hand with no cards in it".
The Baron will not be moved and claims that his charm is more potent than even a post-hypnotic suggestion in conditioning X10's mind to reject anything bad that might be said about him.
X8 tells the story of X11, a French agent who was crippled for life after being beaten by thugs after making similar inquiries into the Baron's personal business.
X2 gets some help with his mission in the form of X12, a former criminal who now acts as an informer for X2 in X13's underworld.
X14 rakes up X15, the Baron's last mistress, who remains bitter at his treatment of her.
She is bent on revenge and will do anything to help X2.
X16 tells X2 that the Baron "collects women" and chronicles his conquests in a book.
X2 realises that this book, written in X8's own hand, is the key to curing X10 of her devotion to the scoundrel.
X16 tells X2 that this book is kept in the Baron's study.
First, X2 goes to see X10, bringing X16 with him, but X10 is proof against X2's words.
X16 then makes it clear that X10 might end up ruined, or murdered, by X8 if she continues.
X10 still stands firm, and the meeting ends with X2 narrowly averting a public scene involving the enraged X16.
Later, X2 is attacked by two of X8's men, and the newspapers imply that he is near death.
X3 goes to X17, only to discover that X2's injuries have been exaggerated to give the impression that he will be out of action for quite a while.
Several days later, X2 is sufficiently recovered to be out of bed.
The Baron is planning a trip to X18 the X19 just before the wedding, and will be leaving in three days.
X2 knows that X8 will take his incriminating book with him, never daring to leave it behind in his study.
X2 orders X3 to learn everything that he can about Chinese pottery in the next 24 hours.
The next day, X2 presents X3 with a fake business card styling him as X20 and an actual piece of X21 pottery, a saucer.
He is to go to X22's house, pose as a connoisseur of Chinese pottery, and try to sell the saucer.
X3 does as X2 tells him, but cannot fool the Baron for very long, and X8 soon realises who has sent him.
As X3 faces his murderous captor, a noise from another room alerts the Baron, and he rushes into his study just in time to see X2 jump out of the window, having stolen the book.
The Baron rushes to the window, but X16, who has been hiding outside, throws oil of vitriol in his face.
X3 applies treatment to his injuries until further assistance comes.
The Baron is now hideously disfigured, but X2 says even this would not break X10's attachment.
When X10 sees the book of conquests, written in her fiancé's handwriting, she is forced to admit she has been wrong.
An announcement in X23 reports the engagement has been called off, and also that vitriol-throwing charges are being pressed against X16.
Extenuating circumstances reduce her sentence to the lowest possible for such an offence.
X7's client is never identified by name, but is strongly hinted to be X24.
X3 spots a royal coat of arms on the carriage bearing him away and hurries to tell X2, who interrupts by saying that the client is "a loyal friend and a chivalrous gentleman.
Let that now and for ever be enough for us."

title: The Adventure of the Three Gables
label: The Adventure of the Three Gables
sentences: The story begins with a visit to X1 from X2, a black man and a cowardly ruffian who warns X3 to keep away from X4.
Although X5 has come to intimidate X6 secures X5's future cooperation by threatening to tell what he knows about the suspicious death X7 involving X5.
X5's boss is X8, and he must be connected with the X9, of which X10 has just learnt from a message from X11, a lady who lives at X12, a house X13.
X14 is an elderly woman whose son has recently died in X15.
He was an attaché there.
Some peculiar things have happened at X12.
X14 has lived there nearly two years and in all that time has attracted very little attention from her neighbours.
Suddenly, however, a man came to her recently and offered to buy her house and all the furniture in it.

She was not really willing to do it, especially after her X16 told her that the legal agreement drawn up by this prospective buyer would forbid her to remove any possessions from the house when she moved out.
As she is telling X10 this story, he becomes aware that someone is eavesdropping on the conversation.
He opens a door and drags in a wheezing maid.
X10 manages to establish that X17 communicated to X8 the fact that her mistress was hiring X3, and that precipitated X2's visit.
X10 also finds out that a rich woman hired X8 and his thugs to do her dirty work.
X17 is also a member of the gang but will not give up all their secrets.
She leaves in a huff.
Obviously, this woman wants something that has come into the house quite recently.
X10, seeing some trunks with Italian placenames on them, realizes that her late X18's belongings must hold the key.
He instructs X14 to try to get X19 to spend a couple of nights at X12, to keep the house guarded.
X10 finds X5 outside, keeping the house under surveillance.
X5 is now inclined to help X10 if he can, to avoid any indiscreet talk about the X20 lad who met his end so tragically.
He swears, however, that he does not know who has hired X8.
The following day, the X12 is burgled, and X10 and X21 go back to investigate.
The burglars chloroformed X14 and stole a manuscript from her son's belongings.
She had managed to grab part of one sheet of paper from it when, coming round, she lunged after one of the thieves.
The police inspector at the scene treats the matter as an ordinary burglary, but X10 knows better.
He examines the bit of manuscript retained by X14, and it appears to be the end of a lurid novel.
X10 is struck by the peculiar wording; the story abruptly changes from third-person narration to first-person narration.
It is in X22's handwriting; so it would seem that he was putting himself in a story that he was writing.
X10 and X21 go to see X23, a wealthy woman who is used to getting what she wants.
The happenings at X12, and the information X10 obtained from X24, "his human book of reference upon all matters of social scandal", have all added up to something.
It turns out that X25 was involved with X23 at one time.
She broke the relationship off, and he almost wrought his revenge by writing a thinly veiled account of their affair, to be published as a novel.
Everyone in X26 would know who the characters truly were, were the novel ever published.
X27 established that no copy had ever been sent to X22's publisher but realized that he must have a copy.
She hired X8 and his confederates to secure the manuscript.
She tried legal means at first, and when that did not work, she resorted to crime.
She has burnt the manuscript.
X10 forces X23 to write a cheque for £5,000 to furnish X14 with a first-class trip round the world in return for his silence about X27's nefarious dealings.

title: The Adventure of the Blanched Soldier
label: The Adventure of the Blanched Soldier
sentences: In January 1903, at X1.
X2 comes to X3 with a strange story regarding his friend, X4.
X2 and X5 served in X6 in X7 during X8.
X5 was sent home after being treated for a bullet wound; hearing nothing from his friend for quite some time afterward, X2 began to suspect something was amiss.
X2 wrote to X9's father, and was told X10 had gone on a voyage round the world for his health.
X2 found it odd that X10 himself had not written to him about this matter, and managed to convince X10's mother to invite him to the X5's family home, X11, near X12.
There were four people there—the colonel and his wife, and an old butler and his wife.
The irritable colonel repeated the story about his son's world voyage, implied X2 was lying about knowing X10, and abruptly refused X2's request for X10's contact information.
That evening, in the ground-floor bedroom, X2 talked to the X13.
After X14 mentioned X10 in the past tense, X2 asked if X10 was dead, to which the butler replied "I wish to God he was, Sir!"
After X14 had left, X2 was considering what the phrase might mean, when he suddenly saw X10's face looking in on him through the window.
X10's skin was blotched white in places, and when he realized he had been spotted, he fled into the night.
X2 pursued him, but stopped after hearing a door slam in the distance.
Determined to solve the mystery, X2 contrived to stay one more night in X11.
While exploring the estate, he met a small, well-dressed man coming out of one of the outbuildings.
The man also indicated X10 had gone away, but X2 later noticed the man watching him suspiciously.
Fearing that X10 was being held against his will in the outbuilding, X2 secretly returned to the building at night and looked through the window.
He spotted the well-dressed man reading a paper in one chair, and X10 sitting in another chair, his back to the window.
At this point, X15 discovered what X2 was up to, berated him for violating the family privacy, and ordered him off the premises.

After hearing X2's story, X3 asks two questions; one, to clarify X10's strange blanched appearance, and two, what sort of paper the well-dressed man was reading, though X2 is uncertain of the answer to the second question.
The two agree to return to X11 in a week's time.
Upon his arrival at X16 observes X14 removing a pair of tarry-smelling leather gloves, indicating the presence of disinfectants.
The colonel threatens to summon the police if X2 and X3 do not leave, but X3 points out that this would make the family secret public.
He writes the word "leprosy" on a piece of paper and shows it to the colonel; realising that X3 knows all, the colonel agrees to grant X3 and X2 an interview with X10.
The young soldier orders them to keep their distance while he tells his story.

When he was wounded in X7, he had dragged himself to a nearby building and slept in a bed there; in the morning, a doctor on the premises found him, and informed him that the building was a leper hospital and that X10 was in danger of catching the disease.
X10 was sent to a regular hospital, and later back home to X17; however, some weeks later, white blotches began to appear on his skin.
Fearing he had caught leprosy, and knowing that he would be forced into segregation in a leper colony if the British authorities found out, X10 and his parents decided that he should hide.
The well-dressed man staying with X10 is X18, a sympathetic local general practitioner who agreed to keep the X5's secret.
The story ends happily.
With X18's permission, X3 brings X19, a famous dermatologist from X20, to see to X10.
X21 determines that X10 is not a leper, but is suffering from ichthyosis, an unsightly but non-contagious treatable disease.

title: The Adventure of the Lion's Mane
label: The Adventure of the Lion's Mane
sentences: In 1907, some time after his retirement to the X1 goes for a walk and meets his friend X2, headmaster of a local preparatory school called "X3".
Shortly thereafter, X4's science teacher, X5, staggers up from the nearby beach, dressed in only his overcoat and trousers.
He collapses at their feet, and dies shortly thereafter, having managed to scream the words "The Lion's Mane".
He has long, narrow welts curving around his body; he appears to have been repeatedly whipped with some sort of thin, flexible scourge, until his weak heart gave out with the pain.
X6, the morose mathematics teacher at the X7, arrives on the scene, having just finished teaching an algebra class.
X8 sends him to find the police, then examines the nearby bathing pool, which had been created by unusually high tides after a recent series of gales from the south.
X8 finds X9's dry, folded towel, and concludes he had not yet been in the water.
There are people far down the beach, and some fishing boats out at sea, but none are close enough to have had anything to do with the tragedy.
The police arrive, but a search of the surrounding caves reveals no clues.
X6, due to his temper, is a possible suspect; he once threw X9's Airedale Terrier through a window.
However, X4 insists the two men were friends.
A note in X9's pocket suggests someone named "X10" had an appointment to meet him, so X4 and X8 go to the house of X11, the daughter of a wealthy sailor-turned-businessman.
As they arrive, X12 passes them, having just left X13's house.
When X12 refuses to tell X4 what he was doing there, the conversation escalates into a sharp argument, and X4 gives X12 notice.
Inside the house, X13's unpleasant father and brother reveal that they both disliked X9 as being below their station.
However, X13 explains that she and X9 were secretly engaged, and often agreed to meet in private.
She also admits that X12 is a former admirer of hers, causing X8 and X4 to believe he may have killed X9 out of jealousy.
Days later, the inquest is adjourned due to lack of evidence.
X12's rooms are searched, in vain.
Later, X9's dog is found dead on the same beach its master died on, a look of extreme pain on its face.
This, and the memory of the dying man's last words, triggers X8 to start a new line of inquiry, and he begins to dig through his old books.
X14 of the X15 visits, and asks if he should arrest X12, but X8 points out that X12 has an alibi.
Suddenly, X12 and X4 burst in, the former in great pain and with his torso covered in the same curving welts X9 had.
After treating X12 with brandy, and applying salad oil to the wounds, X8 leads X4 and X16 back to the bathing pool.
After some intense searching, he finds what he was looking for; a Cyanea capillata, or lion's-mane jellyfish, which has been washed into the pool by the recent gales.
The three men promptly crush it beneath a boulder, killing it.
X12, once recovered, explains that he was swimming when the creature stung him, though he only felt it and did not see it.

sentences: X1, stepmother to the three X2 children – X3, and X4 – and mother to X5, blackmails the family lawyer, X6, into destroying her late husband's second will that would split his fortune between her and his children, leaving them $200,000 each, freeing them from her controlling presence.

title: The January Man
label: The January Man
sentences: On New Year's Eve, X1 socialite X2 returns home from the evening's festivities.

The mayor, frustrated with the lack of progress in the case, tells X3 commissioner X4 to bring in his brother, former detective X5.

X7 talks X6 into returning, but only on the condition that he be able to cook dinner the next night for X7's wife, X8, who is X6's ex-girlfriend.
After a press conference announcing X6's reinstatement, X8 and X6 have dinner.
Old wounds are opened, including mention of a canceled check which indicated that X7 was involved in the scandal that got X6 fired.
After reporting for work, X6 takes a different office than the one he was assigned because the light was not to the liking of his friend X9, a painter.
After getting X10 to add X9 to the payroll as his assistant, X6 begins work on the case.
His first lead is to speak to the mayor's daughter, X11, who was a friend of X12.
After X6 and X11 visit X12's apartment, he decides to let her stay at his apartment because she is too frightened to return to her own.
X6 realizes that the previous murders occurred on dates that are prime numbers, all of which are among the twelve prime numbers possible up to the number 31.
Because 5 is the only one of the prime numbers that has not been used, X6 deduces that the next murder will take place the following night, on the fifth of the month.
However, X6 is seemingly proven wrong when a woman is strangled one day ahead of X6's prediction, after which the killer leaps out the window to his death.
X6 believes that this is a copycat killing, especially when he learns that the man broke a window, as opposed to picking a lock to gain entrance as in the other murders.
X7 and the mayor consider the case closed and are content to be done with X6.
X6 and X9 discover the position of the victims' buildings, when seen on a map of X1, forms the constellation X13.

They also realize that all the rooms in which the murders took place have windows on the front of the building, and that when the exterior positions of the windows are lined up together according to which floor they are on, they correlate to eleven notes in the chorus of the song "X14".

X6 sets a trap with X11 as bait, outfitting her with a neck guard to prevent the killer from strangling her.
The trio stakes out the room in a supply closet and witness the killer picking the lock to get into the apartment.

title: Ten Little Indians (1989 film)

In addition, their host, X1, is absent.
Following their dinner, by means of a gramophone recording, an inhuman voice accuses each person of a murder that they had caused, for which they had escaped justice.

His death mimics the first verse of the English nursery rhyme X6.
One of the ten Indian dolls that adorn the dining table is found with its head snapped off.
In the morning, X4's wife X7 is found dead in her bed (possibly from an overdose), fulfilling the second line of the rhyme.

X4 dies next with an axe buried in his head.

X11 manages to repair the radio and makes contact with the outside; a spotter plane will be sent the next morning.
At night, the terrified remaining guests admit to their guilt.
A storm arrives and X12 dies, shot in the head.
X10 dies with his throat slit.
X13 barricades himself in his tent, only to be found dead the morning after, stabbed in the chest.
By now, only X11 and X14 are left, and X14 turns on X11 with his gun.
He lunges at her and she shoots him.
She returns to the common tent where X12, alive, is waiting, wearing his judicial robes and wig, with a noose prepared for her to fulfil the last verse of the rhyme.
He forces X14 at gunpoint into the noose and explains how X10 helped him fake his own death so he would be free to spy on the rest of the party: the "red herring" from the rhyme.

X12 explains that after being diagnosed with a terminal illness, he planned the safari – his own 'private, big game hunt'.

He pulls the chair out from under X14 and watches her struggle in glee as he drinks poisoned wine to kill himself as well.
He dies and X11 re-appears, alive, only grazed by the bullet X14 shot, and rescues her.

title: After Dark, My Sweet

sentences: Ex-boxer X1 is a drifter and an escapee from a mental hospital.
